item.title: Stellantis, accordo con Wayve può ridurre costi e tempi sviluppo guida autonoma - AD
item.description: L'AD di Stellantis , Antonio Filosa, ha detto che la partnership della casa automobilistica con la startup britannica Wayve potrebbe contribuire a ridurre drasticamente i tempi e i costi di sviluppo dei sistemi avanzati di assistenza alla guida, in un momento in cui i produttori di auto sono in corsa per introdurre sul mercato funzionalità di guida autonoma.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'AD di Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , Antonio Filosa, ha detto che la partnership della casa automobilistica con la startup britannica Wayve potrebbe contribuire a ridurre drasticamente i tempi e i costi di sviluppo dei sistemi avanzati di assistenza alla guida, in un momento in cui i produttori di auto sono in corsa per introdurre sul mercato funzionalità di guida autonoma. Intervenendo insieme del Ceo di Wayve, Alex Kendall, all’evento tecnologico Wave a Torino, Filosa ha sottolineato che la scala di produzione sarà fondamentale per rendere accessibile la guida autonoma e favorirne una più rapida diffusione. "Se la penetrazione seguirà il percorso che riteniamo avverrà su larga scala, la dimensione industriale del settore automobilistico, che rappresenta uno degli asset complementari che portiamo ad Alex, contribuirà a ridurre i costi, un aspetto ovviamente molto importante", ha detto Filosa, riferendosi alla cosiddetta tecnologia di assistenza alla guida di livello 2++, che consente la guida senza mani pur richiedendo la supervisione del conducente. Secondo Filosa, la riduzione dei tempi di sviluppo, attualmente pari a circa 24 mesi per Stellantis, è stata un vantaggio fondamentale della collaborazione con i partner tecnologici. A maggio Stellantis ha annunciato una partnership con Wayve per integrare il software di guida basato sull’intelligenza artificiale della startup nella propria piattaforma STLA AutoDrive. Il lancio del primo prodotto è previsto per il 2028 in Nord America. Nel frattempo, le autorità di regolamentazione europee stanno ancora lavorando per armonizzare le norme di omologazione relative ai sistemi di guida assistita sempre più sofisticati, mentre le case automobilistiche spingono per una diffusione più ampia. CONCORRENZA SEMPRE PIÙ INTENSA Inizialmente i costruttori tradizionali puntavano a sviluppare sistemi avanzati di guida autonoma perlopiù internamente, ma con i costi alle stelle e i ritorni più lenti del previsto, si stanno affidando sempre più spesso ad aziende tech specializzate. Wayve, che collabora anche con altre case automobilistiche, tra cui Nissan (7201.T) e Mercedes (MBGn.DE) , ha detto che la propria tecnologia è progettata per essere implementata su molteplici marchi automobilistici e mercati. Kendall ha affermato che il portafoglio di marchi di Stellantis – che comprende Jeep, Fiat, Peugeot e Maserati – offre un’opportunità unica per adattare le caratteristiche di guida autonoma a veicoli diversi, utilizzando lo stesso sistema di intelligenza artificiale di base. "Uno degli obiettivi… è la varietà di veicoli e marchi di cui dispone Stellantis", ha detto. La partnership nasce in un contesto di crescente concorrenza nel settore della guida automatizzata. Tesla (TSLA.O) sta esercitando pressioni sulle autorità di regolamentazione di tutta Europa affinché approvino la sua tecnologia Full Self-Driving, sostenendo che i sistemi avanzati di assistenza alla guida possano migliorare la sicurezza stradale e accelerare l’adozione di funzionalità autonome. All’evento di Torino, Stellantis e Wayve hanno offerto dimostrazioni di guida senza mani al volante su prototipi di Fiat 500e e Maserati Grecale, ampliando le applicazioni della tecnologia presentata per la prima volta all'inizio dell'anno su una Jeep Grand Cherokee.

item.title: Los países bálticos solicitan a la UE que prohíba el tránsito de cereales rusos
item.description: Lituania, Letonia y Estonia propusieron el viernes, en una carta dirigida al presidente del Consejo Europeo, Antonio Costa, y a la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, que la Unión Europea prohíba las exportaciones de cereales rusos a través del bloque.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lituania, Letonia y Estonia propusieron el viernes, en una carta dirigida al presidente del Consejo Europeo, Antonio Costa, y a la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, que la Unión Europea prohíba las exportaciones de cereales rusos a través del bloque. Los estados bálticos pretenden poner fin a los envíos de cereales rusos a través de sus puertos después de que Moscú intensificara los tránsitos en respuesta a los ataques de Ucrania contra sus puertos del mar Negro. Estonia anunció la semana pasada la primera prohibición. "La UE no debe convertirse en un canal a través del cual Rusia compense las consecuencias económicas de su propia agresión", indicó la carta. El primer ministro estonio, Kristen Michal, tiene la intención de plantear la cuestión en la reunión del Consejo Europeo de la próxima semana, según un comunicado independiente del Gobierno estonio. La embajada rusa en Estonia afirmó en un comunicado enviado por correo electrónico que "las decisiones tomadas por el Gobierno estonio suelen suscitar dudas en los círculos empresariales y entre la sociedad". Las embajadas rusas en Letonia y Lituania no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. El primer ministro lituano, Mindaugas Sinkevicius, propuso el jueves la medida y sugirió además que la UE imponga sanciones a los oligarcas agrícolas rusos que apoyan la guerra en Ucrania. "Lituania propondrá no solo prohibir dicho tránsito, sino también incluir en la lista de personas sancionadas a determinados oligarcas agrícolas rusos que apoyan la guerra", escribió en una publicación en Facebook.

item.title: Verstappen se impone a Russell y logra pole para sprint del Gran Premio de Singapur
item.description: Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, se hizo el viernes con la pole position para la carrera al sprint del Gran Premio de Singapur, superando por poco al piloto de Mercedes George Russell, que le acompañará en la primera fila bajo las luces del Circuito Urbano de Marina Bay.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, se hizo el viernes con la pole position para la carrera al sprint del Gran Premio de Singapur, superando por poco al piloto de Mercedes George Russell, que le acompañará en la primera fila bajo las luces del Circuito Urbano de Marina Bay. Verstappen, que nunca antes había conseguido la pole ni ganado una carrera en Singapur, marcó el mejor tiempo, con un minuto y 31,156 segundos, 0,120 segundos más rápido que Russell. "En Singapur las diferencias son más ajustadas. En la vuelta en sí, das todo lo que crees que puedes dar, rozando los muros en algunos tramos", explicó el piloto holandés. "En cuanto montamos los neumáticos blandos, sentí que el auto cobraba un poco más de vida. Pero no me lo esperaba, así que, por supuesto, estoy muy contento de ser el primero", indicó. "En las últimas carreras hemos estado mucho más fuertes, pero, claro, este circuito sigue poniendo de manifiesto algunas pequeñas debilidades del auto. No obstante, hemos sabido pilotar con ellas lo mejor posible", agregó. Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, fue el tercero más rápido, mientras que el líder del campeonato, Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes —que aventaja a Russell en 84 puntos—, solo pudo ser séptimo. Russell fue el más rápido en la única sesión de entrenamientos celebrada más temprana en la sesión, pero su penalización por la unidad de potencia no afectará a su posición en la parrilla para la carrera al sprint del sábado. Sin embargo, la FIA impuso al británico una penalización de 40 puestos en la parrilla para el domingo, tras haber incurrido en una penalización de 10 puestos por cada uno de los cuatro elementos adicionales de la unidad de potencia, lo que, en la práctica, lo relega al final de la parrilla.

item.title: Verstappen pips Russell to sprint pole at Singapore Grand Prix
item.description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen took pole position for the Singapore Grand Prix sprint race on Friday, pipping Mercedes driver George Russell who will join him on the front row under the lights at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Red Bull's Max Verstappen took pole position for the Singapore Grand Prix sprint race on Friday, pipping Mercedes driver George Russell who will join him on the front row under the lights at the Marina Bay Street Circuit. Verstappen, who had never previously taken pole or won a race in Singapore, set the fastest time of one minute 31.156 seconds, 0.120 seconds quicker than Russell. "It's closer in Singapore. Your lap itself, you're pushing as hard as you think is possible, close to the walls in places," Verstappen said. "Once we bolted on the soft tyres, it felt like the car was coming alive a little bit more. But I did not expect this, so, of course, very happy to be first. "The last few races we've been a lot stronger, but of course this track still highlights a few little weaknesses in the car. But we managed to drive with them as well as possible." Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was third fastest while Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who leads Russell by 84 points, was only seventh quickest. Russell was [USN:L4N45V0BZ TEXT:"fastest in the only practice session"] earlier on Friday but his power unit penalty will not affect his position on the grid for Saturday's sprint. However, the FIA handed the Briton a 40-place grid penalty for Sunday after he incurred a 10-place penalty for each of four additional power-unit elements, effectively consigning him to [USN:L4N45T0QW TEXT:"the back of the grid"].

item.title: Partido Trabalhista derrota Verdes em disputa por cadeira no Parlamento britânico
item.description: O Partido Trabalhista, do primeiro-ministro do Reino Unido, Andy Burnham, venceu nesta sexta-feira a eleição para uma vaga no Parlamento deixada pelo ex-líder Keir Starmer, superando uma forte concorrência do Partido Verde, de esquerda, o que representou um impulso para o primeiro-ministro britânico.
item.dc:creator: Alistair Smout
item.content:encoded: O Partido Trabalhista, do primeiro-ministro do Reino Unido, Andy Burnham, venceu nesta sexta-feira a eleição para uma vaga no Parlamento deixada pelo ex-líder Keir Starmer, superando uma forte concorrência do Partido Verde, de esquerda, o que representou um impulso para o primeiro-ministro britânico. A candidata trabalhista Sagal Abdi-Wali, presidente do conselho municipal, conquistou a vaga no distrito eleitoral de Holborn e St Pancras, no centro de Londres, com 12.292 votos, contra 8.928 de Zack Polanski, líder do Partido Verde. A vitória, que já era esperada, dará ânimo a Burnham, empossado como primeiro-ministro por parlamentares que temiam que a impopularidade de Starmer estivesse abrindo caminho para um desafio do partido populista Reform UK nas próximas eleições nacionais. Depois de perder o apoio da esquerda para os Verdes no início deste ano, o Partido Trabalhista parece ter reconquistado muitos eleitores, um resultado que gerou mais questionamentos sobre a liderança de Polanski, que havia prometido transformar seu partido em um movimento “ecopopulista”. O ex-ator e hipnoterapeuta de 43 anos, que teve algum sucesso em atrair eleitores do Partido Trabalhista antes de Burnham chegar ao poder, tem sido alvo de críticas depois que membros do partido aprovaram uma moção declarando que o sionismo é racismo em sua conferência anual. A medida, que exigia “o estabelecimento de um único Estado palestino democrático em toda a Palestina histórica”, foi criticada por grupos judeus, outros partidos e pela maioria dos deputados do Partido Verde. Polanski não votou na moção. Depois de admitir a derrota na disputadíssima eleição suplementar, Polanski respondeu aos seus críticos, afirmando que permaneceria como líder, e descreveu o resultado como parte da “lua de mel de Andy Burnham”. No entanto, ele não obteve o apoio total da ex-líder do partido, Caroline Lucas, que teve dificuldade em conter sua raiva pelo que ela considerou uma falta de liderança da parte dele em relação à moção sobre o sionismo na conferência da semana passada. Questionada se ele deveria permanecer como líder, ela disse à BBC: “Acho que vamos apenas ver o que acontece nos próximos dias e semanas”. “Quero que ele fale agora sobre o que aconteceu; quero que ele demonstre a liderança que, francamente, faltou no domingo.” Abdi-Wali, do Partido Trabalhista, que chegou ao Reino Unido ainda criança como refugiada da Somália, disse que sua vitória foi uma derrota para “aqueles que buscam nos dividir”. “Temos a responsabilidade de defender o que construímos e passar isso adiante”, disse ela. (Reportagem de Alistair Smout; Reportagem adicional de Elizabeth Piper)

item.title: Protesters clash with police in Brussels as unions and students march
item.description: A small group of protesters clashed with police in Brussels on Friday as union members, joined by hundreds of students, marched as part of a national strike against planned government budget cuts.
item.dc:creator: Marta Fiorin, Bart Biesemans
item.content:encoded: A small group of protesters clashed with police in Brussels on Friday as union members, joined by hundreds of students, marched as part of a national strike against planned government budget cuts. A few dozen masked protesters dressed in black threw rocks and other objects at police, as anti-police slogans echoed through the streets and anti-police graffiti covered nearby walls. Firefighters extinguished several fires, including on buses, while police responded with tear gas, according to Reuters witnesses. The clashes occurred as thousands of protesters took to the streets of the Belgian capital, including students inspired in part by [USN:L6N45V0FM TEXT:"demonstrations in neighbouring France"]. The strike disrupted public transport and air travel, while many schools and childcare facilities were also affected. Among the demonstrators, some carried placards reading "I skipped class to defend class" and "Education is a right, not a privilege." The Belgian walkout is part of a wave of protests sweeping Europe, with students in France and Italy, among other countries, taking to the streets over education funding, while [USN:L8N45U0SP TEXT:"tens of thousands have rallied in Spain"] over a housing crisis. Police said while the march itself, joined by around 30,000 people, passed off peacefully, clashes erupted near Brussels Central Station and in central Brussels where groups threw bottles, bricks, stones and fireworks at police, set fires and damaged public property. Police said officers used water cannon and tear gas to disperse the groups and that 21 people had been detained or arrested, including 13 minors. The strike was called by Belgium's two largest unions, the socialist FGTB/ABVV and Christian CSC/ACV, which oppose government budget measures they say would make workers, pensioners and low-income households bear the burden of efforts to reduce the country's deficit. Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever said on Thursday that painful budget measures were needed now to avert a looming debt and interest-cost spiral that would otherwise leave future generations with a heavy bill. Student groups, [USN:L1N45T0NH TEXT:"whose protests began earlier this month in Liege"] and spread to Brussels on Friday, say they are also protesting rising education costs, overcrowded classrooms and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. "We're not taken into account at all, and no one seems to realise that it's hard for us too, both for workers and for students," said Emilie L'Honneux, a 23-year-old student from Liege. "We're struggling too, and we are the future of this country," she added.

item.title: Príncipe Harry afirma que entrou em depressão ao ponderar sobre seu futuro na realeza
item.description: O príncipe Harry, do Reino Unido, entrou em depressão quando fez uma pausa nas funções reais em 2019, antes de se afastar formalmente, conforme contou em uma transmissão em vídeo sobre o luto, na qual também falou sobre ter se sentido “emocionalmente entorpecido” após a morte de sua mãe.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O príncipe Harry, do Reino Unido, entrou em depressão quando fez uma pausa nas funções reais em 2019, antes de se afastar formalmente, conforme contou em uma transmissão em vídeo sobre o luto, na qual também falou sobre ter se sentido “emocionalmente entorpecido” após a morte de sua mãe. Harry, o filho mais novo do rei Charles, tem falado abertamente sobre suas dificuldades com a saúde mental e sobre como a morte repentina de sua mãe, a princesa Diana, em um acidente de carro quando ele tinha 12 anos, afetou sua vida. “Passei muito tempo emocionalmente entorpecido, em grande parte porque ninguém me disse que ainda era permitido sentir alegria”, disse ele em um videocast da Masterclass intitulado “Redefinindo o Luto: Construindo Resiliência por Meio da Perda”. Ele também relembrou o período estressante em 2019, quando a tensão com o restante da família real estava aumentando, e ele e sua esposa, Meghan, foram para o Canadá para uma pausa de seis semanas a fim de refletir sobre o futuro. “Estando no Canadá, longe do ambiente estressante onde, presumivelmente, meu corpo estava cheio de adrenalina, em dois ou três dias, senti essa queda brusca de adrenalina, algo que eu nunca havia sentido antes”, disse ele, segundo reportagens da mídia. “Era como se eu precisasse de estresse para que a adrenalina fizesse meu cérebro funcionar, porque eu me tornava inútil em casa." "Na verdade, entrei em depressão por cerca de duas semanas e senti que não conseguia funcionar sem adrenalina”, completou. Semanas após suas férias no Canadá, Harry e Meghan voltaram para o Reino Unido, onde foi anunciado que eles deixariam de ser membros ativos da família real. Há dois meses, o casal voltou ao Reino Unido com o filho, o príncipe Archie, de 7 anos, e a filha, a princesa Lilibet, de 5, após seis anos morando na Califórnia. A campanha de conscientização sobre questões de saúde mental é algo que Harry ainda tem em comum com seu irmão, o príncipe William, herdeiro do trono. Os dois mal se falam desde que Harry criticou publicamente sua família repetidas vezes em entrevistas e em seu livro de memórias.

item.title: EU commissioner says recent Turkish actions widen gap with its EU membership goal
item.description: Turkey is moving further away from its objective of joining the European Union because of its recent efforts to crack down on the LGBTQ+ community and limit media freedoms, the EU commissioner for enlargement said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Tuvan Gumrukcu
item.content:encoded: Turkey is moving further away from its objective of joining the European Union because of its recent efforts to crack down on the LGBTQ+ community and limit media freedoms, the EU commissioner for enlargement said on Friday. Turkey has been an official candidate to join the EU since 1999, but its accession has long been frozen over issues ranging from its human rights record to democratic backsliding. Last week, a Turkish court ordered access to independent news outlet T24's website and social media accounts [USN:L6N45M0VP TEXT:"blocked"] after authorities said it had published 118 pieces of content over the past year deemed to constitute "LGBT propaganda". The decision was taken as part of the "My Family is Safe" investigation, a [USN:L8N4580HX TEXT:"widening crackdown"] targeting LGBTQ+ groups which the government says aims to protect children and family values, but which has drawn [USN:L1N45N0XF TEXT:"sharp criticism"] from rights groups and the EU. Speaking to reporters in the northwestern province of Edirne where she attended the opening of an EU-funded railway project, Commissioner Marta Kos said the bloc had a strong interest in developing a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship with Turkey in light of "new realities" in Europe, but that concerns over democratic standards remained. "The latest developments affecting media freedom, the rights of the LGBTQI+ people and local democracy are widening the gap with Turkey's objective of joining the EU," Kos said. The EU's annual enlargement report, due on October 28, will reflect "our serious concerns in these areas", Kos said, adding that she would "not shy away from stating the facts publicly and clearly". There was no immediate Turkish government reaction to Kos' remarks. NEED FOR EU-TURKEY COOPERATION HAS GROWN, KOS SAYS Despite the lack of progress on its membership aspirations, Turkey has been looking to increase cooperation with the EU. It has repeatedly called for the updating of its [USN:L8N3Z10VR TEXT:"customs union"] with the bloc, and has asked to join various EU programmes. These include the Security Action for Europe, or [USN:L6N42G0EN TEXT:"SAFE"], which helps member states to make defence investments, the Single Euro Payments Area initiative, or [USN:L6N3ZM0I0 TEXT:"SEPA"], which facilitates cashless euro bank transfers, and its "[USN:L1N3ZN0FO TEXT:"Made in Europe"]" rules, which are aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing. Kos said conflicts in the region, especially the expansion of the Russia-Ukraine war to the Black Sea, showed the importance and necessity of cooperation with Turkey. "The relevance of Turkey today is significantly higher than it was four or five years back," she said. Kos said the EU had two tracks of work currently ongoing with Turkey, focused on a "targeted update" of the customs union that would require legislative alignment from Ankara. The other focuses on public procurement, which she said was important for Ankara's aim of joining the "Made in Europe" rules.

item.title: IPCA sobe acima do esperado em setembro sob pressão de energia, transportes e alimentos
item.description: A inflação ao consumidor no Brasil subiu mais do que o esperado em setembro, com alta de 0,82% sobre o mês anterior, impactada pelo avanço dos preços de energia, transportes e alimentos, mostraram dados do IBGE nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Viga Gaier
item.content:encoded: A inflação ao consumidor no Brasil subiu mais do que o esperado em setembro, com alta de 0,82% sobre o mês anterior, impactada pelo avanço dos preços de energia, transportes e alimentos, mostraram dados do IBGE nesta sexta-feira. Em 12 meses, o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA) subiu 4,58%, voltando a superar o teto da meta de inflação perseguida pelo Banco Central, mostraram os dados do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística. Pesquisa da Reuters apontou que a expectativa de analistas era de alta de 0,73% do IPCA em setembro, acumulando em 12 meses aumento de 4,50%. O avanço dos preços veio após o IPCA ter registrado em agosto a primeira deflação em um ano (-0,32%), refletindo principalmente uma forte queda nos custos de energia em decorrência da incorporação do chamado Bônus de Itaipu -- valor distribuído a milhões de consumidores anualmente após apuração do saldo registrado na conta de comercialização da energia da usina hidrelétrica binacional no ano anterior. Em setembro, além da saída das contas desse alívio, várias concessionárias de energia reajustaram para cima suas tarifas, e a bandeira amarela -- que incorpora uma tarifação adicional aos consumidores -- seguiu em vigor. No mês, os preços da energia elétrica residencial saltaram 7,98%, representando o principal impacto individual no índice (+0,32 ponto percentual). Já o grupo de preços dos transportes registrou uma inflação de 0,89%, devolvendo a deflação de 0,86% de agosto, refletindo altas em passagens aéreas (9,66%) e combustíveis (1,41%). O grupo alimentação e bebidas teve alta de 0,83%, após três meses consecutivos de queda de preços. Os dois grupos -- transportes e alimentos e bebidas -- tiveram um impacto de 0,18 ponto cada no índice geral. "Os alimentos tiveram problema de oferta em setembro, com mais chuva e mais frio em regiões produtoras do país", disse o gerente da pesquisa do IPCA, Fernando Gonçalves. Ele destacou as altas do tomate (37%) e da batata (24,07%). O índice dos preços dos serviços -- acompanhado de perto pelos economistas -- teve alta de 0,61% em setembro, acelerando ante o aumento de 0,03% no mês anterior. O Banco Central voltará a se reunir para deliberar sobre a taxa básica de juros -- atualmente em 13,75% -- em novembro, e a expectativa predominante no mercado é de um sexto corte consecutivo de 0,25 ponto percentual na Selic. "Observamos uma piora qualitativa do IPCA na margem, com destaque para a aceleração dos núcleos e, principalmente, dos serviços, que seguem rodando em patamar elevado", disse o economista Leonardo Costa, do ASA. "Ainda assim, entendemos que o Banco Central deve manter o processo de flexibilização monetária, apoiado na avaliação de que a inflação tende a convergir de forma mais favorável no horizonte relevante da política monetária", afirmou, acrescentando que a estratégia mais provável segue sendo a de cortes graduais de 0,25 ponto. A inflação foi um tema presente na campanha eleitoral à Presidência, com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição, frisando que o país tem registrado os menores níveis de inflação da história, enquanto seu rival, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), deu ênfase aos níveis de custo de vida elevados. Os dados desta sexta-feira foram divulgados a pouco mais de duas semanas do segundo turno eleitoral no país.

item.title: Wolff desmiente las especulaciones "descerebradas" sobre un posible favoritismo en Mercedes
item.description: El jefe del equipo Mercedes de Fórmula Uno, Toto Wolff, desmintió de forma rotunda los rumores de que su equipo favorece al líder del campeonato, Kimi Antonelli, y tildó a los críticos de "descerebrados", mientras las opciones de George Russell se hunden tras una sanción que le obligará a salir desde la última posición en Singapur.
item.dc:creator: Tom Westbrook
item.content:encoded: El jefe del equipo Mercedes de Fórmula Uno, Toto Wolff, desmintió de forma rotunda los rumores de que su equipo favorece al líder del campeonato, Kimi Antonelli, y tildó a los críticos de "descerebrados", mientras las opciones de George Russell se hunden tras una sanción que le obligará a salir desde la última posición en Singapur. "Son unos descerebrados, quienquiera que piense eso", dijo Wolff a la prensa cuando se le preguntó qué les diría a quienes creen que Antonelli está recibiendo un trato de favor. El piloto italiano, que corre con un monoplaza mejorado en el circuito urbano de Marina Bay, ha ganado ocho carreras esta temporada, frente a las tres de su desafortunado compañero de equipo. Lidera con 84 puntos de ventaja sobre Russell —que se retiró la semana pasada por un fallo en el motor— de cara al Gran Premio de Singapur, donde una sanción por haber agotado los cuatro motores permitidos por el reglamento situará a Russell en la última posición de la parrilla de salida. "Es una auténtica tontería. Siempre he intentado, desde que llegué a la Fórmula Uno, incluso en mi etapa en Williams, ser lo más equilibrado y transparente posible con los pilotos", dijo, recordando una conversación que mantuvo hace años en la parrilla con Alain Prost sobre su archirrival Ayrton Senna. "Le dije: 'Solo por curiosidad, ¿por qué las cosas se torcieron tanto entre tú y Senna?'. Y él respondió: 'Porque nunca sabíamos cuáles eran las intenciones del equipo'". "Así que me lo tomé como un reto para mantener siempre el equilibrio. Y no fue fácil con Lewis y Nico en su momento", afirmó, refiriéndose a la tensión que existía entre los entonces compañeros de equipo Lewis Hamilton y Nico Rosberg en Mercedes, bajo la dirección de Wolff, hace una década. Esta semana, el equipo ha vuelto a equipar a Russell con una configuración del monoplaza anterior en Singapur y marcó el mejor tiempo en la sesión de entrenamientos del viernes. "Tenemos a Kimi desde que tenía 11 años… (y) a George, que lleva con nosotros desde los 17", dijo Wolff. "Estamos muy unidos. Por eso resulta bastante molesto que haya unos lunáticos que, en realidad, no entienden cómo funcionan las relaciones, y que lancen este tipo de acusaciones". "Lo más importante es que George sabe cómo es el equipo y Kimi también lo sabe. Siempre intentaremos darles las mismas oportunidades, y en lo que respecta a la mejora técnica, es un buen ejemplo: no sabemos cuál de los dos va a ser más rápido", agregó.

item.title: UK man charged with plot against Farage motivated by extreme left-wing mindset, prosecutor says
item.description: A British man charged with murdering a former British minister and later charged with a terrorism offence targeting Reform UK leader Nigel Farage was motivated by an extreme left-wing mindset and hostility to Reform, prosecutors said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A British man charged with murdering a former British minister and later charged with a terrorism offence targeting Reform UK leader [USN:L1N45O0PT TEXT:"Nigel Farage"] was motivated by an extreme left-wing mindset and hostility to Reform, prosecutors said on Friday. Joshua Kerry, 28, is charged with the murder of Ann Widdecombe, a prominent figure in Farage's Reform UK party, who prosecutors say was repeatedly hit on the head with a hammer in her home in July. He was subsequently charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of terrorist acts between May 2024 and July this year, accused of carrying out research on prominent people and travelling to, and attempting to gain entry to, Farage's house. Prosecutor Jonathan Polnay said Kerry had compiled a list "that contained the names of politicians and prominent figures" including Farage and Widdecombe. He did not provide any other names. Kerry had an "extreme left-wing and/or an anti-establishment mindset" and also held particular hostility towards Reform, Polnay said. Polnay added that prosecutors would allege that Widdecombe's murder "has a terrorist connection – we say it was politically and ideologically motivated". Kerry, who appeared in court by video link from Belmarsh prison, was not asked to enter any pleas and was remanded in custody until his next hearing in January.

item.title: Liverpool without Isak, Gakpo for heavyweight Man City clash
item.description: Liverpool will be without Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo for Sunday's heavyweight Premier League clash with leaders Manchester City at Anfield, manager Andoni Iraola said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Liverpool will be without Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo for Sunday's heavyweight Premier League clash with leaders Manchester City at Anfield, manager Andoni Iraola said on Friday. Both players returned from international duty with injuries, after Gakpo picked up an ankle injury playing for the Netherlands against Serbia while Isak suffered what Iraola described as a "small" thigh injury with Sweden against Romania. Isak's absence is a significant blow after the striker had finally found his form, scoring four goals in the opening five league games. "Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo will not play the game, they are not ready, they both have injuries in the international break," Iraola said. Neither injury is believed to be long-term, with Gakpo's availability depending on how he copes with the pain while the club monitors both players day by day. Their absence could open the door for 21-year-old Wales forward Lewis Koumas to lead the attack against City. "Koumas has our trust," Iraola said. "I don't think it's a big surprise, I always liked the player and he has already shown in important minutes that he is ready to go and we have also other players who can go in those positions." Iraola said a demanding stretch of games before the next international break in November would provide a significant test of Liverpool's credentials. "I think this run of games we have now (with league and Champions League campaigns resuming), the demands are very high, they are also very condensed, so I think it will say a lot about us," Iraola said. "I think after this run of games, we will really know where we are." City top the table as the only team with a 100% record after five games, while Liverpool are six points behind them in sixth, with two wins and three draws. The rivalry alone would make Sunday's clash a blockbuster, but the spotlight on Anfield will be considerably more intense with City playing for the first time since an independent commission found them guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. A social media post promoting a "Bus greeting" has urged Liverpool supporters to gather near the stadium several hours before kickoff with flags, banners, pyrotechnics and flares ahead of the arrival of the City players' bus. "I think uncertainty is not good for anyone, and anyone involved, but the process is ongoing and we have to be patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end," Iraola said of the case. City have denied any wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal.

item.title: Inflación en Brasil supera rango objetivo en septiembre y excede previsiones antes de balotaje presidencial
item.description: La inflación anual de Brasil se aceleró más de lo previsto en septiembre, superando el rango objetivo del Banco Central, a medida que las presiones sobre los precios se extendían por toda la economía y los costos de los alimentos volvían a crecer, apenas unas semanas antes de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La inflación anual de Brasil se aceleró más de lo previsto en septiembre, superando el rango objetivo del Banco Central, a medida que las presiones sobre los precios se extendían por toda la economía y los costos de los alimentos volvían a crecer, apenas unas semanas antes de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales. El índice de precios al consumidor (IPCA) avanzó un 4,58% en los 12 meses hasta septiembre, según datos de la agencia de estadística IBGE publicados el viernes, frente al 4,22% de agosto, y por sobre la previsión de los economistas del 4,50% en una encuesta de Reuters. En términos mensuales, los precios crecieron un 0,82% en septiembre con respecto a agosto, superando también las expectativas de un aumento del 0,73%. Los nueve grupos analizados registraron subidas en septiembre, y los precios de los alimentos y bebidas, que son objeto de especial atención, subieron un 0,83%, luego de tres descensos mensuales, según el IBGE El Banco Central de Brasil tiene como objetivo mantener la inflación en un rango del 3% más/menos 1,5 puntos porcentuales. El reciente repunte de los precios de los alimentos y el debilitamiento de la moneda local, el real, son argumentos en contra de acelerar los recortes de las tasas de interés, ya que se necesitan nuevas caídas en los servicios y en la inflación subyacente para un ciclo de relajación monetaria más rápido, dijo Andrés Abadía, economista jefe para Latinoamérica de Pantheon Macroeconomics. Los responsables de política monetaria, que en septiembre recortaron la tasa de interés de referencia por quinta reunión consecutiva hasta el 13,75%, se reunirán los días 3 y 4 de noviembre, poco más de una semana después de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil. Los precios al consumidor y los elevados costos de financiación se han convertido en un asunto central de la campaña electoral, en la que el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y el senador Flávio Bolsonaro proponen enfoques contrapuestos.

item.title: Baltic countries seek EU ban on Russian grain transit
item.description: Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia proposed a European Union ban on Friday on Russian grain exports through the bloc in a letter addressed to European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia proposed a European Union ban on Friday on Russian grain exports through the bloc in a letter addressed to European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The Baltic states are [USN:L8N44W17M TEXT:"seeking to end"] shipments of Russian grain through their ports after Moscow [USN:L8N44P0X3 TEXT:"stepped up the transits"] in response to attacks by Ukraine on its Black Sea ports, with Estonia last week [USN:L8N45N0DX TEXT:"announcing the first ban"]. "The EU must not become a channel through which Russia compensates for the economic consequences of its own aggression," the letter read. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal intends to raise the issue at next week's European Council meeting, according to a separate statement from the Estonian government. The Russian embassy in Estonia said in an emailed statement that "decisions made by the Estonian government often raise questions in business circles and among society" The Russian embassies in Latvia and Lithuania did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius [USN:L8N45U0I3 TEXT:"on Thursday proposed"] the measure and also suggested the EU should impose sanctions on Russian agricultural oligarchs who support the war in Ukraine . "Lithuania will propose not only banning such transit but also adding specific Russian agricultural oligarchs who support the war to the list of sanctioned individuals," he wrote in a post on Facebook.

item.content:encoded: Die südafrikanische Juristin Navi Pillay erhält den diesjährigen Friedensnobelpreis. Die 85-Jährige werde für ihren Einsatz für Frieden und Völkerrecht geehrt, teilte das norwegische Nobelkomitee am Freitag in Oslo mit. Pillay war unter anderem Richterin am Internationalen Strafgerichtshof (IStGH) und leitete eine UN-Untersuchungskommission, die Israel Völkermord im Gazastreifen vorwarf. Die Vergabe an Pillay unterstreiche die Bedeutung einer regelbasierten internationalen Ordnung, hieß es in der Begründung des Komitees. Das Völkerrecht stehe unter enormem Druck und seine Institutionen würden angegriffen. "Wir sehen eine Entwicklung hin zu einer Machtpolitik auf Kosten rechtlicher Rahmenbedingungen und des weltweiten Respekts vor Recht und Gerechtigkeit", erklärte das Komitee. Wann immer Macht vor Recht gehe, untergrabe dies die Stabilität, das Vertrauen und das friedliche Zusammenleben. Obwohl das Nobelkomitee weder Israel noch US-Präsident Donald Trump namentlich erwähnte, gilt die Entscheidung als politisch hochbrisant. Der IStGH in Den Haag steht seit Längerem im Visier Trumps, der seine Kampagne gegen das Gericht verschärft hat, nachdem dieses im vergangenen Jahr Haftbefehle gegen den israelischen Ministerpräsidenten Benjamin Netanjahu erlassen hatte. Israel verurteilte die Preisvergabe scharf. "Die Entscheidung des Nobelkomitees ist beschämend und eine Unterstützung für Antisemiten wie Pillay selbst", sagte der israelische UN-Botschafter in Genf, Daniel Meron, der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Als Vorsitzende der UN-Untersuchungskommission habe sie Kampagnen angeführt, die die Existenz Israels untergrabe, den Terrorismus verharmlose und die Realität im Dienste einer politischen Agenda manipuliert habe. Israel wies den UN-Bericht nach seiner Veröffentlichung im vergangenen Jahr als "skandalös" und "erfunden" zurück. "EINE BESONDERE VERANTWORTUNG" Pillay erfuhr von der Auszeichnung während einer Juristenkonferenz in Nürnberg. Sie hielt sich in dem Gebäude auf, in dem 1945 und 1946 die Nürnberger Prozesse gegen führende Vertreter des NS-Regimes geführt wurden – genau 80 Jahre und neun Tage nach den dortigen Urteilsverkündungen. "Als Letztes habe ich den Bericht über Gaza übergeben, in dem das Geschehen dort als Völkermord bezeichnet wird", sagte Pillay vor einer feiernden Menge, wie ein Video in den sozialen Medien zeigte. Mit Blick auf die letztjährige Preisträgerin María Corina Machado, die ihre Medaille im Januar an Donald Trump übergab, scherzte Pillay unter dem Gelächter der Anwesenden: "Wenn Sie noch ein bisschen mehr klatschen, teile ich diesen Preis vielleicht mit Trump." Später widmete sie die Auszeichnung allen Überlebenden internationaler Verbrechen sowie den Verteidigern der internationalen Justiz, deren Mitgefühl und Mut dafür sorgten, dass Verbrechen nicht ungestraft bleiben. An die Staats- und Regierungschefs der Welt gerichtet sagte sie: "Sie sind rechtlich verpflichtet, die Menschenrechte zu schützen und auf Krieg zu verzichten." Die Präsidentin des IStGH, Tomoko Akane, begrüßte die Entscheidung. "In einer Zeit tiefgreifender Herausforderungen für die internationale Rechtsordnung und die Rechtsstaatlichkeit ist diese Anerkennung von besonderer Bedeutung", erklärte sie. Trump forderte im vergangenen Monat andere Länder auf, den IStGH zu verlassen, und verhängte Sanktionen gegen Richter und Staatsanwälte. Jorgen Watne Frydnes, der Vorsitzende des Nobelkomitees, sagte zu Reuters, dass die Institutionen weltweit unter Beschuss stünden und Richter sanktioniert würden. "Die mächtigsten Staaten tragen hierbei eine besondere Verantwortung", sagte er. INDISCH-TAMILISCHE HERKUNFT Die Bundesregierung gratulierte Pillay zur Auszeichnung. Der stellvertretende Regierungssprecher Stefan Meyer sagte in Berlin, Pillay habe über Jahrzehnte hinweg mit großem persönlichen Engagement für Menschenrechte, Gerechtigkeit und die Durchsetzung des Völkerrechts gekämpft. Ihr Lebenswerk vom Einsatz gegen die Apartheid bis zu ihrer Arbeit für die internationale Strafgerichtsbarkeit und die Vereinten Nationen verdiene höchste Anerkennung. Deutschland stehe fest zum Völkerrecht. "Wir gehören zu den wichtigsten Unterstützern des Internationalen Strafgerichtshofs und setzen uns für starke, unabhängige und handlungsfähige internationale Gerichte ein", sagte Meyer. Pillay wurde in Durban in der damaligen südafrikanischen Provinz Natal als Tochter einer indisch-tamilischen Familie geboren. 1967 eröffnete sie als erste Frau in Natal eine eigene Anwaltskanzlei und war später die erste nicht-weiße Richterin am Hohen Gerichtshof des Landes. In ihrer Karriere verteidigte sie unter anderem Nelson Mandela und andere Gegner des Apartheid-Regimes. Von 2008 bis 2014 war sie UN-Hochkommissarin für Menschenrechte. Sie ist die fünfte südafrikanische Persönlichkeit, die den Friedensnobelpreis erhält. Derzeit ist sie zudem als Richterin am Internationalen Gerichtshof (IGH) im Völkermord-Verfahren gegen Myanmar tätig. Der Friedensnobelpreis ist mit zwölf Millionen schwedischen Kronen (rund 1,2 Millionen Dollar) dotiert. Er wird am 10. Dezember, dem Todestag des Preisstifters Alfred Nobel, in Oslo überreicht.

item.title: Disagreements over UN climate report
item.description: Hello!
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hello! Thank you to all of you Switchies for sending such positive feedback and interacting with yesterday’s newsletter on data centres. [USN:L6N45U0S1 TEXT:"Click here"] to revisit part one of my deep dive on whether data centres can be built sustainably and stay tuned for part two next Thursday. Today’s newsletter is all about climate policy and whether our planet is headed in the right direction. It will move from disputes in the world’s top climate body about releasing the latest scientific review on a warming planet to an exploration of how one country’s politics can turn the tide. There will also be an urgent plea from this year’s COP31 hosts. Tensions are high, and so is the world’s temperature. Let’s start with the disputes from the world’s leading authority on climate change, where members of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) still can’t agree on a timeline to publish its next review of the latest science on the warming planet after nearly three years of debate. The impasse over publication dates could leave countries to decide the next phase of action without consensus on critical issues – including the extent to which some global warming might be reversible – according to interviews with more than a dozen current and former IPCC scientists, government negotiators and meeting observers. [USN:L6N45U1A0 TEXT:"Click here"] to read the full exclusive story. Over in Brazil, the [USN:L6N45U0TV TEXT:"tight presidential election"] has some investors, executives and climate-focused businesses worried that a government led by conservative Senator Flavio Bolsonaro may not maintain the policies underpinning its emerging green economy. Bolsonaro[USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:" topped the first-round vote"] on the weekend with a stronger-than-expected performance, after a campaign in which he promised to strengthen the regulated carbon market but did not criticize the climate track record of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, under whom deforestation soared. Additionally, a study by [USN:L1N45U0UP TEXT:"climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima"] found that Brazil's next Congress is likely to pose a greater obstacle to legislation to protect the environment after elections this month. The study found that almost 70% of elected lawmakers have little or no commitment to environmental issues. Meanwhile, Murat Kurum, [USN:L1N45U06N TEXT:"Turkey's climate minister "]and president of this year's UN climate conference, COP31, urged delegates at a pre-COP meeting in Fiji to focus on restricting global warming, stating that the "1.5-degree goal ... is a matter of survival". "Today is a time where everyone is running away from responsibility," Kurum told a press conference. "We do not have a single minute, a single day to lose." He said countries needed to protect oceans and get better access to funding for resilience projects. The UN Environment Programme has said holding warming beneath 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels is impossible in the near term but could be achieved over time with emissions reduction. * Climate Buzz Tropical Storm Simon expected to become a major category-4 hurricane Storm Simon is forecast to rapidly strengthen into [USN:L1N45U0Y9 TEXT:"a "very dangerous" category-4"] hurricane before striking Mexico's Pacific coast this weekend, according to the US National Hurricane Center. It said Simon was likely to become a hurricane with destructive winds of 65 mph (100 kph) and life-threatening flooding. Is it here yet? The US, China and Japan’s El Niño weather predictions The [USN:P8N45007N TEXT:"US Climate Prediction Center"] said El Niño continues to strengthen, with a greater than 83% chance that a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January to March 2027. [USN:L6N45V0FI TEXT:"China's National Climate Centre"] said that a super El Niño event officially formed last month, after rapid warming of the Pacific Ocean from May to September. Meanwhile, [USN:P8N44I067 TEXT:"Japan's weather bureau"] said that the El Niño phenomenon has strengthened to its strongest on record since September, adding that there was a 100% chance the conditions will continue into the Northern Hemisphere by winter. [USN:L6N45F0NL TEXT:"Click here"] to revisit the Reuters El Niño explainer. Asia races to speed up renewables in response to Iran war Members of the [USN:L1N45U0G6 TEXT:"Association of Southeast Asian Nations"] have pledged to increase the share of clean energy in power generation in response to energy supply risks laid bare by the Iran war. Renewables make up 14.1% of primary energy, well short of a 2025 target of 25%, while green power has made up 33.7% of total capacity since 2020 against a 2025 target of 35%, according to a recent ASEAN energy outlook. US sued over plan to blast Utah canyon inscribed by Black American ‘Buffalo Soldiers’ Conservation groups sued the US Bureau of Land Management over plans to replace a winding dirt track with a paved road through Gate Canyon in eastern Utah. The blast would destroy 100-foot (30-metre) cliffs covered in historic inscriptions near world-renowned Native rock art. There are also 19th-century inscriptions by Black American "Buffalo Soldiers" in the US Army and European pioneers, according to the lawsuit. [USN:L6N45U1CG TEXT:"Click here"] for the full Reuters report. Thousands of European wind and solar power systems exposed online Thousands of [USN:L6N45S0LR TEXT:"wind and solar power administrative systems"] in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned. The findings come amid concerns about Europe's critical infrastructure, which has faced suspected sabotage and cyberattacks frequently attributed by Western governments to Russia since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russia denies any involvement. * What to Watch From the suburbs of Virginia to the outskirts of Amsterdam and Dublin, people around the world have increasingly rebelled against the spread of artificial intelligence data centres due to concerns around noise, surging electricity consumption, water stress and industrialization of residential neighbourhoods. The same tale is unfolding in India where major tech giants Amazon, Google and Meta are planning to build their data centres in Mumbai. [USN:L1N45R0Y9 TEXT:"Click here"] to read more about the United States’ clean energy surge. * Climate Spotlight Today’s climate spotlight shines on a 194-year-old tortoise which may unlock secrets to the fountain of youth. The [USN:L6N45S0SM TEXT:"world's oldest-known terrestrial animal"], an Aldabra giant tortoise named Jonathan, may owe his extraordinary longevity to a combination of genetic traits and an ability to keep key cellular systems functioning in a more youthful way, according to scientists. * Number of the Week $178 million That’s how much damage [USN:L6N45T095 TEXT:"Thailand's industrial sector"] has suffered from floods that have swept through parts of the country since last month, according to Secretary-General Panitarn Pavarolavidya of the Federation of Thai Industries. item.title: Pilgrim's Pride forms special committee to review meatpacker JBS buyout bid
item.description: Pilgrim's Pride Corp said on Friday its board has formed a special committee of independent directors to evaluate majority shareholder JBS's unsolicited bid to acquire the remaining shares of the US poultry producer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pilgrim's Pride Corp (PPC.O) said on Friday its board has formed a special committee of independent directors to evaluate majority shareholder JBS's unsolicited bid to acquire the remaining shares of the US poultry producer. One of the world's largest meatpackers disclosed in August it [USN:L4N44F1FA TEXT:"wanted to acquire"] the Pilgrim's Pride shares it did not already own, seeking full control and a delisting of the company. JBS, which already owned about 82%, offered 2.086 Class A shares, or $28.49, per Pilgrim's Pride share in its proposal — in line with the stock's closing price that day. The special committee has appointed Ropes & Gray LLP as legal counsel and Moelis & Company LLC as financial adviser to assist in reviewing the proposal, Pilgrim's Pride said. The company said its board would not approve the proposed transaction without a favorable recommendation from the special committee. It added there was no assurance that a definitive agreement would be reached or that any transaction would ultimately be completed. Shares of the company last closed at $28.50, giving it a market capitalization of $6.79 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: Mayoría de habitantes de Gaza necesita refugio ante amenaza de inundaciones por El Niño, según la ONU
item.description: Casi toda la población de Gaza necesita tiendas de campaña o ayuda para conseguir refugio de cara al invierno, ya que se prevé que el fenómeno meteorológico de El Niño traiga lluvias más intensas, mientras los suministros siguen siendo escasos debido a las restricciones israelíes, dijo el viernes la ONU.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Casi toda la población de Gaza necesita tiendas de campaña o ayuda para conseguir refugio de cara al invierno, ya que se prevé que el fenómeno meteorológico de El Niño traiga lluvias más intensas, mientras los suministros siguen siendo escasos debido a las restricciones israelíes, dijo el viernes la ONU. El Niño —que podría ser el más intenso de la historia, según la agencia meteorológica de la ONU— podría debilitar aún más los edificios inseguros y provocar inundaciones, dado el grave deterioro de los sistemas de drenaje del enclave, señaló la agencia de Naciones Unidas para las migraciones, OIM. Casi dos millones de personas en el enclave, devastado en gran medida por la guerra lanzada por Israel en respuesta al ataque de Hamás en octubre de 2023, necesitan asistencia, pero los actores humanitarios solo han cubierto alrededor del 17% de las necesidades de suministros para refugios de invierno, señaló la directora general de la OIM, Amy Pope. "Las familias que ya han sufrido desplazamientos repetidos y pérdidas devastadoras deben poder afrontar el invierno con seguridad y dignidad", afirmó Pope, añadiendo que las restricciones impuestas por las autoridades israelíes están dificultando que las agencias amplíen sus respuestas. Las autoridades israelíes no han permitido la entrada en Gaza de unos 8.600 kits de refugio de emergencia, que incluyen madera, una lona y algunos materiales básicos, al considerarlos de doble uso, según la OIM. El COGAT, el organismo militar israelí que supervisa los flujos de ayuda hacia Gaza, no respondió de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios de Reuters. Israel alega motivos de seguridad para justificar sus restricciones en Gaza. La OIM señaló que había podido introducir algunas lonas y tiendas de campaña, pero que no era suficiente para cubrir las necesidades actuales en Gaza. Más de la mitad de todas las tiendas de campaña y refugios improvisados del enclave deben ser sustituidos, ya que se encuentran en mal estado, señaló la OIM, advirtiendo que hay pocas alternativas dado que los edificios dañados por la guerra suponen un riesgo para la seguridad. En agosto se identificaron más de 3.600 estructuras como peligrosas y con riesgo de derrumbe, mientras que alrededor de 1,8 millones de personas viven en campamentos de desplazados, la mayoría en zonas con riesgo de inundaciones, según la OIM.

item.title: SONDEO Precios minoristas de Argentina se habrían acelerado levemente en septiembre
item.description: El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina habría anotado una variación mediana de 1,9% en el noveno mes del año traccionado por factores estacionales que impactaron en el segmento de alimentos, según expresaron analistas a Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Hernan Nessi
item.content:encoded: El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina habría anotado una variación mediana de 1,9% en el noveno mes del año traccionado por factores estacionales que impactaron en el segmento de alimentos, según expresaron analistas a Reuters. El Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) dará a conocer el dato oficial del IPC de septiembre el próximo martes (1900 GMT), contra una variación del 1,7% de agosto y en línea a la leve aceleración esperada. "El comportamiento del mes estuvo fuertemente influenciado por factores estacionales", afirmó la consultora C&T Asesores Económicos. Y añadió que el rubro "'Alimentos y bebidas' aumentó 2%, el mayor ritmo desde mayo, pero con gran influencia de las verduras, otro componente estacional, que trepó 11%. Hubo además mayor dinamismo en la carne, que aumentó 2,1%". Las estimaciones entre 14 analistas locales y extranjeros arrojaron una variación promedio de igual porcentaje para el IPC del noveno mes. El rango de estimaciones osciló entre una variación mínima de 1,4% y una máxima de 2,1%. Fuentes consultadas por Reuters no prevén que la inflación para los próximos meses sea inferior al registro de agosto último. "No creemos que el proceso de desinflación vuelva a los niveles de comienzos de año en ausencia de volatilidad cambiaria, pero seguramente fluctuará cerca del 1,7%-2% durante los próximos meses", expresó Ignacio Ruiz, economista de la consultora Ecolatina. Y explicó que esto sería "producto no solamente del ajuste constante en servicios públicos, sino también de bienes estacionales -habrá que seguir como afecta 'El Niño' la oferta de diversos productos- y de una mayor demanda que tendrá lugar en la medida que poco a poco se recupere el crédito y el salario real". Por otra parte, 13 analistas encuestados esperan que la inflación interanual en septiembre registre un 33,3% según la mediana de las estimaciones, contra una proyección de 33,5% del mes previo. El reciente [USN:L1N45S11P TEXT:"Relevamiento de Expectativas de Mercado (REM)"] realizado por el banco central argentino (BCRA) entre consultoras, centros de investigación locales e internacionales y entidades financieras arrojó que se espera un IPC de 30% para 2026. El Gobierno libertario de Javier Milei se esfuerza por reducir la inflación, frente a una contracción de la economía con aumento de la pobreza e indigencia. "Según nuestro 'nowcast' la inflación de septiembre finalizaría en 2% mensual, lo cual llevaría la inflación interanual al 33,4%", dijo a Reuters Julián Neufeld, economista de la Fundación Libertad y Progreso. "Para lo que queda del año, prevemos una inflación que oscile en torno al 2%, pero que en promedio esté por debajo de ese número. Con esto en mente, estaríamos hablando de cerrar 2026 con una inflación del 30%", agregó.

item.title: Cineasta da Caxemira Arfat Sheikh é libertado da detenção pelo ICE nos EUA, segundo campanha
item.description: O premiado cineasta da Caxemira Arfat Sheikh foi libertado sob fiança na quinta-feira da detenção do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega dos EUA (ICE), após ter sido detido em 24 de setembro, de acordo com um comunicado divulgado por uma campanha organizada por seus amigos e familiares para libertá-lo.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O premiado cineasta da Caxemira Arfat Sheikh foi libertado sob fiança na quinta-feira da detenção do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega dos EUA (ICE), após ter sido detido em 24 de setembro, de acordo com um comunicado divulgado por uma campanha organizada por seus amigos e familiares para libertá-lo. Sheikh, cujo trabalho tem explorado o conflito na Caxemira administrada pela Índia, sua terra natal, foi detido pelo ICE, órgão do Departamento de Segurança Interna (DHS), ao desembarcar de um voo vindo da Califórnia no Aeroporto Internacional de Washington Dulles, informou a campanha. A campanha informou que a fiança de Sheikh foi concedida na terça-feira e ele foi liberado na quinta-feira, acrescentando que o processo de deportação contra ele continua. De acordo com a campanha, Sheikh, que morava em Alexandria, Virgínia, entrou nos EUA em 2019 com um visto de estudante para cursar pós-graduação em cinema na Georgia State University e solicitou asilo em 2020. A campanha afirmou que ele tinha um pedido de imigração pendente e estava autorizado a trabalhar e morar nos EUA. O Departamento de Segurança Interna disse na quarta-feira que Sheikh foi preso em 24 de setembro. Segundo o órgão, Sheikh “entrou legalmente nos EUA de forma temporária e permaneceu no país ilegalmente após o término de sua admissão legal”. Um pedido pendente não confere status legal nos EUA, afirmou o DHS, acrescentando que ele terá direito ao devido processo legal. O governo do presidente Donald Trump disse em agosto que estava trabalhando “para identificar e revogar os vistos de não imigrante de estrangeiros que vieram aos EUA alegando ser visitantes de curta duração, mas que depois solicitam asilo para permanecer aqui permanentemente”. Trump tem promovido uma repressão à imigração e uma campanha de deportação que, segundo ele, visa melhorar a segurança interna. Defensores dos direitos humanos afirmam que a repressão tem violado o devido processo legal e os direitos à liberdade de expressão, além de ter criado um ambiente inseguro, especialmente para as minorias étnicas, que têm manifestado preocupações com o perfilamento racial.

item.title: Primera victoria de Red Bull con su motor de F1, un triunfo de la convicción para su artífice
item.description: El responsable de sistemas de propulsión de Red Bull, Ben Hodgkinson, prefiere hablar de confianza más que de expectativas tras la histórica primera victoria de la escudería como fabricante de motores de Fórmula Uno.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: El responsable de sistemas de propulsión de Red Bull, Ben Hodgkinson, prefiere hablar de confianza más que de expectativas tras la histórica primera victoria de la escudería como fabricante de motores de Fórmula Uno. La victoria de Max Verstappen, partiendo desde la pole position y con vuelta rápida incluida, en el Gran Premio de Baréin del pasado fin de semana en Malasia se produjo en la decimosexta carrera de la era de las nuevas normas de la F1. La hazaña superó las expectativas de quienes dudaban de que la marca de bebidas energéticas pudiera igualar a potencias consolidadas como Mercedes y Ferrari al construir desde cero una de las unidades de potencia más complejas de la historia de este deporte. Sepang también supuso la primera pole de 2026 conseguida por un monoplaza que no montaba un motor Mercedes, pero Hodgkinson se mostró cauto ante un exceso de optimismo cuando se le preguntó por las expectativas. "Hemos ganado una carrera. Una de dieciséis", afirmó a Reuters antes del Gran Premio de Singapur de este fin de semana y de la 250ª partida del tetracampeón Verstappen. "Creo que 'expectativa' es una palabra peligrosa para cualquier ingeniero de Fórmula Uno. En cuanto empiezas a subestimar a la competencia, es cuando empiezas a perder. Todo el proyecto (del motor) se construyó con la convicción de que esto era posible. Así que lo creí. No lo esperaba", comentó. "AUDAZ Y ATREVIDO" El camino desde el centro de ingeniería hasta la realidad del circuito no ha sido fácil para Red Bull, que dominó en épocas anteriores con motores suministrados por otros. "Ha habido muchos momentos a lo largo del camino en los que parecía que las cosas no iban muy bien. Y conseguir finalmente ponerlo todo en marcha para lograr esa victoria fue, sin duda, un momento muy especial", afirmó Hodgkinson desde su despacho en la fábrica de Milton Keynes. "Mucha gente no creía que fuéramos a estar en esta posición. Otros equipos, miembros de la prensa, probablemente incluso miembros de nuestra propia familia, pensaban que nos estábamos embarcando en algo bastante extremo", agregó. "Pero la mentalidad colectiva y algo que me ha parecido realmente único en Red Bull es la voluntad de emprender proyectos audaces y atrevidos y demostrar que todo el mundo se equivocaba", indicó. Red Bull tuvo que empezar de cero, contratando a expertos de otros equipos, mientras que sus rivales podían centrarse exclusivamente en fabricar un sistema de propulsión a partir de las instalaciones ya existentes. Los recién llegados Audi y los que regresan Honda aún están muy lejos de contar con un paquete ganador. Mercedes ha ganado 11 de las 16 carreras, Ferrari y McLaren dos cada uno, y tan solo el mes pasado el exjefe del equipo Haas, Guenther Steiner, afirmaba que no veía a Red Bull ganando este año. Hodgkinson, que llegó procedente de Mercedes, afirmó que esas dudas fueron "leña para nuestro fuego". "Hay algo en este proyecto que es muy propio de Red Bull", dijo. "Ya sabes, la 'simple empresa de refrescos' que se atreve a fabricar tanto el grupo motopropulsor como el chasis". "Es algo que, en mi opinión, probablemente solo alguien como Red Bull se atrevería a hacer. Y se llevó a cabo con la ambición de querer lograr algo grandioso desde el primer momento", afirmó. PUNTO DE REFERENCIA Red Bull es la única escudería con sede en Reino Unido que cuenta con la producción de la unidad de potencia y el chasis en las mismas instalaciones, mientras que Mercedes tiene sus operaciones repartidas entre Brackley y Brixworth. Ford es socio de Red Bull y Hodgkinson afirmó que la ayuda del gigante automovilístico estadounidense en materia de personal, instalaciones y fabricación fue inestimable. Aunque lo de Sepang fue una sorpresa, posiblemente favorecida por el firme del circuito y, sin duda, por el hecho de que Verstappen alcanzara otro nivel, el motor ya había marcado la pauta, hasta el punto de que la FIA, como organismo regulador, lo declaró el punto de referencia con el que se debe evaluar a los demás. Las unidades de potencia de 2026 se reparten en una proporción de 53-47 entre combustión y electricidad, y el equilibrio se inclinará más hacia la primera en los próximos años. "Creo que obsesionarse demasiado con el mejor motor es algo a lo que el reglamento casi te obliga (…) pero en realidad lo que importa es tu ritmo general", afirmó Hodgkinson cuando se le preguntó si el suyo era realmente el mejor. "A veces puedes tomar decisiones sobre los motores que, en realidad, reducirían su rendimiento, pero que, en conjunto, hacen que el auto vaya más rápido. Por eso nos medimos por nuestro rendimiento en pista", señaló. "Estoy muy orgulloso de lo que hemos conseguido", añadió, levantando de su escritorio una taza con el eslogan "Red Bull, mejor con hielo", un doble sentido que podría referirse tanto al motor de combustión interna como a la bebida. "Eso es todo. Tengo una taza que lo demuestra".

item.title: India central bank to sell $2.6 bln of bonds, tighten bank reserve need to squeeze cash
item.description: India's central bank announced the next leg of open market bond sales and tightened daily maintenance of cash reserve ratio on Friday in a bid to further drain rupee liquidity from the banking system.
item.dc:creator: Dharamraj Dhutia
item.content:encoded: India's central bank announced the next leg of open market bond sales and tightened daily maintenance of cash reserve ratio on Friday in a bid to further drain rupee liquidity from the banking system. The Reserve Bank of India will sell 250 billion rupees ($2.58 billion) of bonds on Tuesday through open market operations, an effective liquidity-draining tool. The regulator also mandated that banks would need to maintain 99% of the daily CRR from October 16 against 90% earlier. The moves come days after the RBI raised its key policy rate for the first time in nearly four years and signalled more rate hikes. The central bank did not announce any liquidity draining measures in the policy. RBI Governor [USN:L4N45T0GV TEXT:"Sanjay Malhotra"] said the surge in liquidity would not be a long-term phenomenon and a large amount of liquidity would get absorbed within this financial year the ends in March. Last month, the RBI [USN:L4N45K0OD TEXT:"sold bonds"] worth 1 trillion rupees, the highest net sale in over a decade. Markets should be prepared for the liquidity surplus to fall below 1% of deposits and potentially lie in the 0%-0.5% of deposits range in the coming quarters, ICICI Securities Primary Dealership said in a note. "OMO sales have led to bear flattening of the yield curve," the primary dealer said. India's banking system liquidity surplus has averaged more than 7 trillion rupees ($72.37 billion) on a daily basis from September 1, amounting to 2.6% of deposits. The RBI will sell bonds maturing from fiscal 2030 to fiscal 2035, including 7.88% 2030, 6.10% 2031, 7.95% 2032, 7.26% 2033, 7.18% 2033 and 7.10% 2034 notes. Banks park 3% of their deposits with the RBI under CRR, and do not earn any income on these funds. ($1 = 96.7300 Indian rupees)

item.title: What is the low-band spectrum that SpaceX acquired for Starlink Mobile
item.description: SpaceX has agreed to acquire a nationwide portfolio of licenses in the low-band spectrum in a deal reportedly valued at $8 billion, as it looks to expand beyond satellite internet and become a serious competitor in the US mobile market.
item.dc:creator: Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: SpaceX (SPCX.O) has [USN:L6N45U1AK TEXT:"agreed"] to acquire a nationwide portfolio of licenses in the low-band spectrum in a deal reportedly valued at $8 billion, as it looks to expand beyond satellite internet and become a serious competitor in the US mobile market. The company first disclosed its plans to enter the mobile services sector during its inaugural earnings call in August. The announcement [USN:L1N4420CG TEXT:"briefly weighed"] on shares of the three major US wireless carriers - AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon - as investors assessed the potential competitive threat. WHAT IS LOW-BAND SPECTRUM? Low-band spectrum refers to airwaves that can travel farther and penetrate buildings better than higher frequencies, making them useful for broad-area mobile coverage. This differs from mid- and high-band spectrum, which can carry more data at a faster speed but cover less area. SpaceX has agreed to acquire up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz low-band spectrum licenses from Grain Management, with plans to develop a hybrid architecture for Starlink Mobile that combines terrestrial infrastructure with satellite connectivity. HOW DOES THE US SPECTRUM LICENSING SYSTEM WORK? Commercial spectrum is a scarce resource in the US, regulated by the Federal Communications Commission, which typically assigns licenses for specific frequencies and geographic areas through auctions or other authorized processes. License holders must comply with technical rules and deployment requirements, but before that comes the transfer of licenses, which generally requires regulatory approval. The latest SpaceX deal for spectrum licenses is awaiting FCC approval. WHAT SPECTRUM DO THE THREE MAJOR CARRIERS HOLD? AT&T's low-band portfolio includes 700 MHz and 850 MHz spectrum, as well as 600 MHz licenses acquired through its July EchoStar deal. Verizon holds spectrum in the 700 MHz and 850 MHz bands, while T-Mobile's low-band holdings include 600 MHz and 700 MHz spectrum. WHAT IS THE PLAN FOR STARLINK MOBILE? The company plans to integrate the spectrum into its next-generation satellite system, while also deploying ground-based radios and antennas on towers and rooftops. The FCC approved Starlink Mobile's Gen2 constellation application this week, authorizing SpaceX to launch 15,000 satellites optimized for 2 GHz spectrum worldwide.

item.title: Germany wants a seat in ECB's governing bodies, finmin says
item.description: Germany wants to continue to be "strongly represented" in the European Central Bank's governing bodies in the future, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on Friday in Luxembourg on the sidelines of a finance ministers meeting.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany wants to continue to be "strongly represented" in the European Central Bank's governing bodies in the future, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on Friday in Luxembourg on the sidelines of a finance ministers meeting. "I am coordinating closely with the Federal Chancellery on all issues concerning the ECB, and of course, we will put forward a German candidate," Klingbeil said. Euro zone finance ministers on Thursday started a process to replace European Central Bank board [USN:L8N45U1U5 TEXT:"member Isabel Schnabel"], who will leave the ECB on January 3 to take up a post at the International Monetary Fund. "In the bilateral discussions here, I have noticed that every colleague is very clear that Germany plays a role at the ECB," Klingbeil added.

item.title: In parched Hungary, volunteers build their own dams to hold onto vanishing water
item.description: In a bone-dry valley in Hungary, forest workers and volunteers piled up terraces of logs and deadwood, hoping to catch any trickles of water that make it down the hillside when the rains finally come.
item.dc:creator: Marton Monus, Krisztina Than
item.content:encoded: In a bone-dry valley in Hungary, forest workers and volunteers piled up terraces of logs and deadwood, hoping to catch any trickles of water that make it down the hillside when the rains finally come. In other areas, other groups fanned out, building barriers across streams and small creeks — their own man-made "beaver dams" designed to pool water and prepare the landscape for an even hotter, drier future. As of this week, they were still waiting for that rain after a drought-hit summer that brought river levels to [USN:L8N4490NK TEXT:"record lows"], disrupting everything from cargo barges to the country's Paks [USN:L8N4490NK TEXT:"nuclear plant"], which relies on flows of cooling water from the Danube. But the teams working under the banner of the grassroots, volunteer "Water Guardians Movement" kept on building, getting ready. 'WE CAN IMPROVE THE SITUATION' "The wells (on my farm) have practically run dry," said Bence Bardos, a forest engineer leading the team building terraces in the Ladany valley in eastern Hungary near the border with Slovakia. "This is the impact from climate change and our special geography in the Carpathian basin." There was little locals could do about that, he said. "But we can improve the situation by small steps, by reversing the water runoff and drainage," the 36-year-old added. The volunteers are turning out in their hundreds to help the country build structures to retain rainwater and restore wetlands — techniques that mark a sharp turnaround from the past, when programmes focused on managing floods, not droughts. Nearly a quarter of the country lies on floodplains, and experts spent decades draining wetlands and building canals to channel water away from the fields and open up more land for agriculture. "We have regulated our rivers, cutting their bends, which means the rivers flow faster, which drains ground water nearby," Diana Ürge-Vorsatz, a professor at the Central European University in Vienna, said. Much of that now needed to go into reverse. The important thing now was to "restore the original natural conditions as much as possible, to allow rivers to flow on longer routes and thus slower, and retain ground water in the winter-spring," Ürge-Vorsatz added. The government announced a new strategy in August which prioritised "natural water retention methods" and, far from draining fields, said some farmland should be deliberately flooded. RESEARCHERS 'CAN'T PERFORM A RAIN DANCE' Agriculture, one of the planks of Hungary's economy, has borne the brunt of the drier conditions. Many farmers have [USN:L8N44T097 TEXT:"given up on maize"] and shifted to alternatives, as researchers work on drought-resistant varieties. This was the first year when the harvested area of maize in Hungary fell below the area planted with sunflowers, said Zoltan Kende, associate professor at the Institute of Agronomy at the MATE University. But even sunflowers have suffered from the drought. "We have shown that dry weather alters the fatty acid composition of sunflowers, resulting in a change in oil quality," Kende added. Researchers could not "perform a rain dance" but there were recommendations they could make on cultivation and other methods to help adaptation, he said. "For each cultivated plant species, we investigate the optimal factors as for temperature, moisture ... that result in the fastest germination. This approach helps enhance resilience against drought damage." Hungary's central bank has said the drought damage to agriculture would cut economic growth by 0.4 percentage points in 2026. The challenges were already there to see as the volunteers worked on the slopes of Ladany valley. Borbala Kanizsay, who was there with her husband, said the creek that ran past their nearby house ran dry in May for the first time she could remember. Most of her parched trees shed their leaves in July. A "terrible sight," the 41-year-old added. "We must adapt to this situation that our climate has changed, and we must strive to keep Hungary a liveable place."
