item.title: EU ministers reach watered down compromise on centralised cap markets supervision
item.description: European Union finance ministers agreed on Friday a scaled-back compromise to centralise supervision of most EU stock exchanges, central counterparties and securities depositories as they seek to make the EU capital markets work better.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: European Union finance ministers agreed on Friday a scaled-back compromise to centralise supervision of most EU stock exchanges, central counterparties and securities depositories as they seek to make the EU capital markets work better. The deal aims to reduce the fragmentation of 27 different legal systems government capital flows and make the EU more attractive to innovative companies, which now often choose to relocate to the United States. But it differs from the original proposal for the Market Integration and Supervision Package made by the European Commission. That envisaged all stock exchanges, large central counterparties (CCPs) and central securities depositories (CSDs) being supervised by the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) in Paris, rather than by national authorities as now. "People can hold out for the perfect, or people can hold hands and jump together with the good," said Simon Harris, finance minister of Ireland, who was in charge of negotiating the compromise. The idea behind the single supervisor was to help apply the same EU laws in the same way across all countries, eliminating national interpretations to reduce costs and bureaucracy. But Germany refused to support the proposal unless its Deutsche Boerse stock exchange remained under local German supervision. The compromise introduces trading thresholds and geographical footprint criteria that would allow the German stock exchange to be exempt from ESMA oversight. The criteria also exclude Swiss exchange operator SIX Group, which has the Madrid bourse and Aquis, as well as French-owned Tradition and Deutsche Boerse-owned electronic trading platform Tradegate (T2GG.F) . The compromise also removed three out of the original nine CCPs from under ESMA's jurisdiction — the Dutch CBOE Clear, Spain's BME and Sweden's Nasdaq Clearing. The initial 15 CSDs that were to fall under ESMA were reduced to 13, with Spain's Iberclear and the Baltic's Nasdaq CSD removed. Only between 10 to 15 from around 360 crypto-asset service providers in the EU will be subject to ESMA oversight, officials said. Smaller EU countries also won concessions that give national supervisors greater influence in ESMA decision-making. Negotiations on the final shape of the law will continue with the European Parliament, once the EU legislature reaches its own position on the issue.

item.title: Maioria bipartidária nos EUA atribui aumento dos custos a políticas de Trump, aponta Reuters/Ipsos
item.description: Cerca de 78% dos norte-americanos atribuem às políticas do presidente Donald Trump o aumento dos preços, que está superando o crescimento de seus rendimentos, de acordo com uma pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos que revelou que a maioria dos republicanos e democratas cita o custo de vida como sua principal preocupação antes das eleições de meio de mandato do próximo mês.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cerca de 78% dos norte-americanos atribuem às políticas do presidente Donald Trump o aumento dos preços, que está superando o crescimento de seus rendimentos, de acordo com uma pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos que revelou que a maioria dos republicanos e democratas cita o custo de vida como sua principal preocupação antes das eleições de meio de mandato do próximo mês. Cinquenta e sete por cento dos republicanos afirmaram que os custos vêm crescendo mais rapidamente do que seus salários, um exemplo gritante de como a busca de Trump por tarifas de importação, guerra com o Irã e outras políticas entraram em conflito com uma promessa central de campanha para 2024: acabar com a inflação e reduzir os preços “desde o primeiro dia”. Em vez disso, a inflação aumentou, a ponto de o Federal Reserve dos EUA ter mudado de rumo para aumentos nas taxas de juros a fim de conter os aumentos de preços que os formuladores de políticas atribuíram a uma variedade de fatores, incluindo o aumento dos custos globais de energia após o início da guerra com o Irã e a imposição de impostos agressivos sobre as importações pelo governo. As preocupações com a economia e a guerra levaram a aprovação pública de Trump a níveis recordes de baixa e têm pesado sobre o apoio ao seu Partido Republicano antes da eleição de 3 de novembro, que determinará o controle do Congresso pelos próximos dois anos. Cerca de um em cada quatro republicanos desaprova a maneira como Trump lidou com a economia, opinião compartilhada por 63% dos independentes e 92% dos democratas. A desaprovação foi ainda mais acentuada no que diz respeito à inflação, com 68% de todos os entrevistados e 40% dos republicanos insatisfeitos. Jeffrey Talley, de 65 anos, um auditor bancário aposentado de Mission Hills, no Kansas, é um republicano registrado que afirmou ter votado em Trump em 2016, mas não em 2020 nem em 2024, e agora planeja votar no democrata Adam Hamilton naquilo que se tornou uma disputa pelo Senado inesperadamente acirrada no Estado. “Sou totalmente contra todo esse absurdo que está acontecendo no Oriente Médio com a guerra contra o Irã e o aumento do preço da gasolina... isso tem sido muito desanimador”, disse Talley. Ele vê a eleição como uma chance de eleger “alguém que possa exercer um freio e contrapeso à loucura que está acontecendo na Casa Branca”. A pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos, realizada online em todo o país durante seis dias e concluída na segunda-feira, coletou respostas de 4.506 adultos norte-americanos. Ela teve uma margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais para os norte-americanos em geral e de 3 pontos para republicanos, democratas e independentes.

item.title: China, EU reach hybrid vehicle trade understanding, keep talks alive on EV dispute
item.description: China and the European Union reached an "understanding" on trade in hybrid vehicles, the Chinese commerce ministry said on Friday, after two days of talks in which the bloc sought to reduce its trade deficit with Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China and the European Union reached an "understanding" on trade in hybrid vehicles, the Chinese commerce ministry said on Friday, after two days of talks in which the bloc sought to reduce its trade deficit with Beijing. European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic has said he was seeking "[USN:L6N4500OS TEXT:"tangible results"]" from his visit to China, amid the bloc's growing concerns over the gap, which amounted to over €1 billion ($1.12 billion) a day. The understanding on hybrid vehicle trade in a WTO-compliant manner followed intensive negotiations, the Chinese ministry said, without giving details. Asked whether the Chinese statement was a joint one, the European Commission said Sefcovic would comment on the talks at a press conference at 1300 GMT. CHINESE CAR IMPORTS TO EU HAVE RISEN SHARPLY EU officials are concerned by the sharp rise in car imports from China. Imports of plug-in hybrids into the EU have increased 86% in the year to September, with a 20% decline in prices. More than half of these vehicles are now from China, while for 2025, China's share of PHEV imports was 30% in value terms. The discussions between Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and Sefcovic in Beijing on Thursday and Friday were "pragmatic and productive," the Chinese ministry said. China and the EU also agreed to continue discussions on price undertakings and review procedures related to the EU's anti-subsidy investigation into Chinese electric vehicles, according to the ministry. China and EU's dispute over cheap Chinese EV exports, dating to 2024, has clouded bilateral ties, and has since broadened to include sectors such as brandy, pork and dairy, as well as rare earths and critical minerals. China needs foreign buyers for the flood of cheap, state-subsidised goods its own shoppers can't absorb, and the EU is torn between welcoming those imports to ease living costs and keeping them out to rebuild its own factories. Both sides will keep exploring the possibility of lowering tariffs on certain goods within the framework of WTO rules, and continue their dialogue on market access for medical devices, the Chinese ministry said. A third regular meeting of their consultation mechanism will take place in March 2027, and the two sides agreed to maintain communication, including a ministerial-level video conference in January, the ministry said. item.content:encoded: Die Deutsche Bahn und die Bundesregierung drosseln das Tempo bei der Sanierung des maroden Schienennetzes, um für mehr Verlässlichkeit bei den Bauarbeiten und im Zugverkehr zu sorgen. Bis 2031 sollen nur noch 13 statt der bisher geplanten 21 Hauptstrecken grundlegend modernisiert werden, wie das Bundesverkehrsministerium und der Staatskonzern(DBN.UL) am Freitag mitteilten. "Die Idee der Korridorsanierungen ist richtig", sagte Bundesverkehrsminister Steffen Bilger. "In der Vergangenheit hat die Umsetzung jedoch zu oft nicht die gewünschten Ergebnisse gebracht." Deshalb ziehe man jetzt Konsequenzen. Künftig müsse der Bahnbetrieb nach Sanierungen spürbar verlässlicher und pünktlicher werden. "Dafür konzentrieren wir uns auf weniger Korridore, setzen klarere Vorgaben für die Digitalisierung und verlangen eine bessere Planung der Bauvorhaben sowie der Umleitungsverkehre für den Personen- und Güterverkehr", sagte der CDU-Politiker. Die Maßnahme soll die umfangreichen Bauarbeiten verlässlicher machen und die knappen Kapazitäten im Schienennetz berücksichtigen. Bahn-Chefin Evelyn Palla erklärte, man habe aus den ersten Sanierungen gelernt. "Wir wollen die Sanierungen effizienter umsetzen und vor allem die Belastungen für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden während der Bauarbeiten so gering wie möglich halten." Kern der neuen Strategie ist ein Fünf-Punkte-Plan. Dieser sieht unter anderem ein besseres Vorbereiten von Umleitungsstrecken und eine schrittweise Inbetriebnahme der sanierten Korridore vor. Zudem soll das digitale europäische Zugsicherheitssystem ETCS zum neuen Standard werden. Bei jeder Sanierung soll die Technik künftig vorbereitet und ab Anfang der 2030er-Jahre direkt verbaut werden. "ENDLICH KONSEQUENZEN AUS FEHLERN BISHERIGER SANIERUNGEN" Das neue Konzept sei zu kaum mehr geeignet, als den Bundeshaushalt zu entlasten, sagte Bahn-Experte Matthias Gastel von den Grünen der "Rheinischen Post". "Pünktlicher werden die Züge auf weiter modernisierungsbedürftiger Infrastruktur nicht." Die Konkurrenz im Güterverkehr hat in der Vergangenheit die langwierigen Sanierungen kritisiert. Die Geschäftsführerin des Verbands der Güterbahnen, Neele Wesseln, begrüßte, dass Bund und Bahn "endlich Konsequenzen aus den Fehlern der bisherigen Korridorsanierungen ziehen". Irritierend sei aber, dass Bilger sich bereits bei der Branche für eine gemeinsam erarbeitete, tragfähige Lösung bedanke, obwohl der Dialog der Branche gerade erst begonnen habe. "Wir wollen nicht nachträglich eine Lösung abnicken, sondern ihre Ausgestaltung mitbestimmen." Rückendeckung für das Umsteuern kommt von Unions-Fraktionsvize Stephan Stracke. Bauzeiten müssten realistisch geplant und eingehalten, Ersatzverkehre verlässlich organisiert werden, sagte der CSU-Politiker der "Rheinischen Post". "Die zeitliche Streckung der Korridorsanierungen sorgt dafür, dass all dies künftig besser funktionieren kann.". Das sei man den Menschen schuldig, "die tagtäglich auf den Zug angewiesen sind". Die Sanierungen werden den Angaben zufolge nicht gestrichen, sondern nur zeitlich verschoben. Den Zeitplan für die Großbaustellen ab 2032 soll es erst im nächsten Jahr geben. Für 2027 sind Arbeiten an den Strecken Lehrte-Berlin, Rosenheim-Salzburg und Fulda-Hanau geplant. 2029 etwa sollen unter anderem die wichtigen Verbindungen Hamburg-Hannover und Aachen-Köln folgen. Nach Abschluss der jeweiligen Baustelle sollen die Strecken danach "möglichst bis zu zehn Jahre weitgehend frei von größeren baubedingten Einschränkungen" bleiben. Trotz der Probleme bei der Umsetzung verteidigten Bahn und Regierung das Grundprinzip der Generalsanierungen. Auf der sanierten Riedbahn zwischen Frankfurt und Mannheim etwa fahren den Angaben zufolge Züge nun 20 Prozent pünktlicher aus dem Abschnitt heraus, als sie hineinfahren. Auf der Strecke Nürnberg-Regensburg seien die Störungen durch die Infrastruktur seit Abschluss der Arbeiten um über 90 Prozent zurückgegangen.

item.title: Hurkacz hands Djokovic early Shanghai exit with first win over Serb
item.description: Poland's Hubert Hurkacz beat Novak Djokovic for the first time as he dumped the four-times champion out of the Shanghai Masters with a 6-4 6-3 second-round victory on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Poland's Hubert Hurkacz beat Novak Djokovic for the first time as he dumped the four-times champion out of the Shanghai Masters with a 6-4 6-3 second-round victory on Friday. Tenth seed Djokovic arrived in Shanghai fresh from winning a [USN:L6N45S0UI TEXT:"record seventh China Open"] crown after Australia's Alex de Minaur retired with a groin injury in Tuesday's final. The 24-times Grand Slam champion, whose last Shanghai title came in 2018, had an 8-0 record against 29-year-old Hurkacz. But the Pole, a former world number six, produced a clinical display, firing 13 aces and 28 winners while conceding little on serve to beat Djokovic in one hour and 27 minutes in his first Shanghai appearance since capturing the title in 2023. Hurkacz, who missed the tournament in 2024 and 2025, extended his winning streak in Shanghai to eight matches and now faces either Italy's Lorenzo Musetti or China's Zhou Yi. The defeat marked the latest setback in a testing season for the 39-year-old Serbian, who suffered a shock first-round exit at the US Open, his earliest Grand Slam defeat since the 2006 Australian Open. "I was not close to what I was playing in Beijing," Djokovic said. "I'm slightly more tired, not fresh ... "I didn't feel myself on the court in terms of feeling the ball. It's a super quick surface, completely different from Beijing. "If you lose your serve, it is enough to lose the match, once per set, and that is what happened. It is very difficult to return his serve, almost impossible. So yeah, I did not adjust and it was a really tough draw for me, playing him in the first match." Djokovic will now turn his attention to the European indoor swing, with next month's Paris Masters looming. He is ninth in the race for a spot at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin. "I am planning on only playing in Paris, so let's see. Hopefully I can have a good result there," he added. TOP SEED ZVEREV MARCHES ON French and US Open champion Zverev remained firmly on track in Shanghai in his bid to secure the year-end world number one ranking by seeing off local favourite Wu Yibing 6-4 7-6(4). The German world number two can ensure he will reach the pinnacle by the end of the year if he makes the semi-finals or if his nearest challengers Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton lose at any stage of the Masters 1000 tournament. [USN:L1N45S0CV TEXT:"Jannik Sinner"] is currently the top-ranked player, but the Italian ended his season prematurely due to inflammation in his knee and will drop the points he earned for winning the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters and the ATP Finals last year. The only blemish on an otherwise perfect day for top seed Zverev was a minor injury scare at 5-5 in the second set, when the 29-year-old slipped and fell near the baseline and then clutched his left ankle. Memories of the serious ankle injury he suffered in the 2022 French Open semi-finals briefly resurfaced but Zverev recovered and completed the win in the ensuing tiebreak to book a meeting with Frenchman Quentin Halys. Earlier, US Open runner-up Shelton celebrated his 24th birthday with a 6-3 7-6(6) win over German Daniel Altmaier but it was the end of the road for Roland Garros finalist Flavio Cobolli, who fell 6-1 4-6 6-3 to Frenchman Adrian Mannarino.

item.title: Renoir paintings stolen from Riviera museum recovered, six people arrested
item.description: Two Renoir paintings worth millions of dollars that were stolen from a museum on the French Riviera a month ago have been recovered and six suspects have been arrested, the local mayor said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two Renoir paintings worth millions of dollars that were stolen from a museum on the French Riviera a month ago have been recovered and six suspects have been arrested, the local mayor said on Friday. Thieves had [USN:L8N4500AJ TEXT:"broken into"] the grounds of the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer early in the morning of September 8 through a hole cut in a garden fence and entered through a window. The two paintings by Pierre-Auguste Renoir, an Impressionist whose works have fetched tens of millions of dollars at auction, were "Madame Colonna Romano" and "Young Woman at the Well". Both belong to Paris' Orsay Museum and were on loan. "This news is a source of immense joy and a great relief for the town of Cagnes-sur-Mer and its residents," mayor Bryan Masson said in a statement. The Marseille public prosecutor's office did not immediately respond to questions about how the paintings had been recovered. The mayor scheduled a press conference on Thursday afternoon then cancelled it so as not to interfere with the investigation. The thieves had also snatched two other paintings, "Madame Pichon" and "Coco Reading", a portrayal of Claude, Renoir's young son. But they dropped them in the gardens as police, alerted by alarms, arrived and gave chase.

item.title: India's Jio Platforms targets $106 billion valuation in IPO, sources say
item.description: Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms is targeting a valuation of 10.3 trillion rupees ($106 billion) in what would be the country's biggest listing, four bankers on the deal said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Vibhuti Sharma, Kane Wu, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms is targeting a valuation of 10.3 trillion rupees ($106 billion) in what would be the country's biggest [USN:L4N45R0BH TEXT:"listing"], four bankers on the deal said on Friday. Jio Platforms, which counts Meta (META.O) and Google among its major foreign investors, is set to price its shares at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees apiece, the sources told Reuters. The IPO would raise about 302 billion rupees ($3.1 billion) at the upper end of the price band, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's (HYUN.NS) $2.9 billion issue in 2024. The sources were not authorised to speak to media and declined to be named. Reliance did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Bloomberg reported the details of the IPO price band and valuations earlier in the day. Jio's IPO follows the high-profile listing of the [USN:L4N45G0A8 TEXT:"National Stock Exchange of India"] (NSEI.BO) in September, underscoring investor appetite for large offerings in the Indian market. Year-to-date IPO proceeds in India rose 8.3% to $12.65 billion compared with the same period last year, LSEG data shows. A successful listing would place Jio Platforms among the top four Indian listed companies by market capitalisation, behind parent Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) , rival Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and the country's largest private lender HDFC Bank (HDBK.NS) . The IPO valuation is below the $131 billion expected in [USN:L1N42R0B2 TEXT:"June"] when the draft papers for the offering were filed. Analysts said the lower IPO pricing was likely due to a broader correction in the secondary market driven by an Iran war-related spike in crude oil prices. India's benchmark stock index Nifty 50 (.NSEI) has dropped around 6% in nearly four months since then. Jio, led by Mukesh Ambani's son Akash Ambani, operates Reliance's telecom and digital businesses, spanning mobile services, fixed broadband, cloud, entertainment, enterprise technology and AI offerings. The company plans to use up to 275 billion rupees of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. The company's telecom arm had 524.4 million customers as of March. Revenue from operations rose 14.6% to 1.47 trillion rupees in the fiscal year ended March, while profit increased 15.1% to 300.5 billion rupees. ($1 = 96.7300 Indian rupees)

item.title: US-based Kalitta Air orders Airbus freighter jets, sources say
item.description: US military and commercial freight contractor Kalitta Air has ordered eight Airbus A350F freighters as it looks beyond long-time supplier Boeing to tap European capacity for the first time, three people familiar with the order said.
item.dc:creator: Tim Hepher, Dan Catchpole, Allison Lampert
item.content:encoded: US military and commercial freight contractor Kalitta Air has ordered eight Airbus (AIR.PA) A350F freighters as it looks beyond long-time supplier Boeing (BA.N) to tap European capacity for the first time, three people familiar with the order said. Airbus, which declined to comment on any commercial discussions, posted the deal as a firm contract in a recent orders update without identifying the buyer, the people said. Michigan-based Kalitta Air said it was evaluating the jet but had yet to make a decision. "Kalitta Air is evaluating the Airbus A350F platform as part of our long-term fleet planning," an airline spokesperson said. "At this time, we remain in the evaluation phase and have no aircraft order to announce." Founded in 2000 by drag-racing legend Conrad "Connie" Kalitta, the airline traces its roots to a business he set up in 1967 to transport car parts in his own self-piloted Cessna. It now has a fleet of more than two dozen Boeing 747 and 777 freighters working scheduled and one-off cargo charter flights for customers including the Pentagon and US Postal Service. Long dominated by Boeing, the market for air freighters is heating up after Airbus launched the A350F to challenge the out-of-production Boeing 747 and two versions of the Boeing 777. Airbus data shows an order for eight freighters on August 31 without identifying the buyer. That is a common practice whenever airlines want to shield their expansion plans from rivals for as long as possible. One of the people said an airline's decision to expand its fleet could typically be used as a bargaining chip in pilot negotiations, meaning there was no incentive to make it public. A spokesperson for the Air Line Pilots Association, which represents Kalitta Air pilots, said its members had been in negotiations with the carrier's management since late 2024.

item.title: EU aviation body widens Saudi airspace warning after Houthi strikes
item.description: Europe's EASA aviation safety body said on Friday it had expanded the area of Saudi Arabian airspace where it recommended airlines not to operate, after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Riyadh airport.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Lo Nostro
item.content:encoded: Europe's EASA aviation safety body said on Friday it had expanded the area of Saudi Arabian airspace where it recommended airlines not to operate, after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis [USN:L1N45U0A3 TEXT:"attacked Riyadh airport"]. In an update to a conflict zone information bulletin [USN:L1N45M0PB TEXT:"first issued"] on September 30, the EU regulator said recent attacks demonstrated the Houthis' ability and intent to strike targets deeper inside Saudi territory, including the capital. EASA added an area in northwestern Saudi Arabia to the advisory. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said earlier on Friday that [USN:L1N45V06F TEXT:"three Saudi nationals"] were killed and several people were injured in two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday. The Houthis have renewed threats against airlines flying to Saudi Arabia and said on Thursday they had struck the capital's airport with two cruise missiles. "These recurrent missile and drone attacks, together with the activation of air-defence systems, create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft, as well as risks associated with missile and drone overflights, interception activity and falling debris," EASA said. OPSGROUP, a membership-based organisation with almost 10,000 aviation professionals that shares flight risk information, sent a "do not fly" warning for Saudi Arabia to its members on Friday, citing risks of sustained missile attacks and "misjudgment" in defensive responses. "We now recommend avoiding operations in Saudi Arabia entirely, including the use of Saudi airports as en route alternates," it said in the memo shared with Reuters. LUFTHANSA, INDIAN AIRLINES SUSPEND FLIGHTS Following Thursday's attacks, Lufthansa Group and three Indian airlines said they would [USN:L6N45U10R TEXT:"suspend flights"] to Riyadh expected in the coming days. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh is Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah. It handled 296,800 flights in 2025, equivalent to about 813 a day, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority for Statistics. Global flight tracker FlightRadar24 showed 131 flights to and from Riyadh had been cancelled by 1305 GMT on Friday after hundreds of cancellations the previous day.

item.title: Lessor Avolon orders 250 Boeing, Airbus jets with option for 100 more
item.description: Global leasing giant Avolon said on Friday it had agreed to order 140 aircraft from Boeing and 110 from Airbus , with an option to buy a further 100 jets from the European planemaker.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Global leasing giant Avolon said on Friday it had agreed to order 140 aircraft from Boeing (BA.N) and 110 from Airbus (AIR.PA) , with an option to buy a further 100 jets from the European planemaker. The orders were the largest Avolon, the world's third-biggest aircraft lessor, has placed with either manufacturer and bring its total number of aircraft on order to 749, on top of the 561 it currently owns. Dublin-based Avolon said the order comprised 140 Boeing 737 MAX jets, 75 Airbus A320neo planes and 35 of its wide-body A330neos, with options for a further 100 unspecified Airbus aircraft. Aircraft lessors own around half the world's airline fleet and have been in hot demand from airlines in recent years due to a backlog of plane orders, a trend that has supported the specialist industry's rentals, resale values and profits. It has also allowed leading lessors like Avolon to sell their older planes to make room for more fuel-efficient new-technology aircraft. Avolon said in a trading update on Friday that it had sold 29 aircraft during the July-September quarter, with a further 112 aircraft agreed for sale at the end of September. "We continue to see strong demand for new-technology aircraft, reflected in our placement and trading activity this quarter," Avolon CEO Andy Cronin said in a statement. The new orders are subject to approval by Avolon's majority shareholder, China's Bohai Leasing Co Ltd (000415.SZ) , which the lessor said is expected before the end of this month.

item.title: Blindness treatment based on Nobel-winning research shows promise
item.description: It's Nobel Prize season and today we feature promising early results of a novel technique for treating blindness that made Nobel laureates of three scientists this week. We also report on two studies comparing treatment options presented at the American Society for Radiation Oncology meeting.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: It's Nobel Prize season and today we feature promising early results of a novel technique for treating blindness that made Nobel laureates of three scientists this week. We also report on two studies comparing treatment options presented at the American Society for Radiation Oncology meeting. NOBEL-WINNING THERAPY SHOWS EARLY PROMISE IN BLIND PATIENTS Patients with blindness due to retinitis pigmentosa who received a treatment based on research that won the 2026 [USN:S8N44O00U TEXT:"Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine"] had their ability to detect objects restored in a small trial that demonstrated the potential of the novel approach. So-called optogenetic therapy uses light to control brain cells. In the study, researchers combined gene therapy that made surviving retinal ganglion cells sensitive to light with delivery of light to stimulate these cells. The 10 trial participants each received an injection into one eye carrying genetic instructions for ChrimsonR, a light-sensitive protein from GenSight Biologics (SIGHT.PA) . Patients then wore goggles that captured visual information, converted it into patterns of light at wavelengths that activated ChrimsonR in the modified retinal cells, and sent the patterns of light back to the eye. Seven patients became more sensitive to light, with six achieving clinically meaningful improvements, such as being able to detect when an object was present, determine where it was located and reach toward it accurately. One severe adverse event occurred immediately after injection and resolved within minutes, researchers reported in The New England Journal of Medicine . While larger studies are needed to definitively prove the usefulness of ChrimsonR and the goggles, the findings show that even at a very advanced stage of blindness, surviving retinal ganglion cells can be made responsive to light and transmit visual information to the brain, the researchers said. "Even in people with profound vision loss, the visual system retains a remarkable capacity to process new information," study leader Dr. José-Alain Sahel of the University of Pittsburgh said in a statement. RADIATION EFFECTIVE AS SURGERY FOR LOCALIZED PROSTATE CANCER Radiotherapy kept localized prostate cancer under control just as well as surgery, with fewer side effects, researchers reported at the recent American Society for Radiation Oncology , or ASTRO, meeting in Boston. After a median of eight years of following patients, survival without recurrence was statistically similar. Of those who received five sessions of stereotactic body radiation therapy delivered over two weeks, 91% were alive without cancer recurrence versus 84% after surgery. SBRT delivers the radiation directly to the prostate while limiting exposure to nearby healthy tissue. The trial involved 123 patients, most with low- or intermediate-risk cancers who were monitored for reappearance of a tumor or a rise in prostate-specific antigen levels, a potential indicator of prostate cancer. The trial’s original goal was to compare quality of life after the interventions. Efforts to enroll nearly twice as many participants were thwarted by the COVID pandemic, leaving the study with too few patients to answer that question. Because it was not designed to establish noninferiority for cancer control, the trial cannot prove the treatments are equivalent for this outcome. “What we can say is that... we have mature data showing excellent cancer outcomes with five-treatment radiotherapy,” study leader Dr. Nicholas van As of The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust in the UK said in a statement. A separate analysis presented at ASTRO found that patient-reported sexual-function scores declined in both groups but remained significantly better after the radiation therapy. Median erectile-function scores on a 25-point scale, where higher scores indicate better function, were 19 with SBRT and 5 for prostatectomy after five years. Also at five years, 8.3% of SBRT patients were using urinary pads for leaks, compared with 48% of surgery patients. AVOIDING WHOLE-BRAIN RADIATION IN RARE LUNG CANCER Patients with an uncommon, aggressive form of lung cancer who develop brain metastases can benefit from a safer radiotherapy technique that is already standard for common lung tumors, according to data from a study reported at ASTRO . Stereotactic radiosurgery uses high-dose radiation beams to destroy brain tumors without surgical incisions and with minimal damage to nearby brain tissues. It is already the preferred treatment for brain metastases from most other tumors. Small cell lung cancer has been an exception for fear that treating only visible tumors could leave cancer cells behind. As a result, patients undergo whole-brain radiation, increasing their risks for memory loss and other cognitive declines. In the trial, 151 patients received either stereotactic radiosurgery or a modern form of whole-brain radiation. Patients lived a median of 17 months after focused stereotactic radiosurgery versus nine months following whole-brain radiotherapy. The trial was designed to assess the length of time before patients experienced cognitive decline from each treatment method. The researchers found no significant difference, possibly because of protection afforded by the newer form of whole-brain radiation, they said. Comparisons of cognitive outcomes may also have been complicated by fewer whole-brain radiation patients alive for later follow-up. While prolonged survival was not the trial's primary goal and cannot be proved by this study, the results show how far both approaches have come, principal investigator Dr. Vinai Gondi of the Northwestern Medicine West Region and Proton Center in Warrenville, Illinois, said in a statement. “For patients with small cell lung cancer, we now have two modern radiation therapy strategies to consider and randomized evidence to help us understand how best to use them,” Gondi said. item.title: IKEA's Danish stores could become shelters as Europe boosts preparedness
item.description: In the bedding department of Denmark's largest IKEA store, security chief Torben Mortensen walks past rows of display beds and describes a use for them far removed from retail: emergency shelter.
item.dc:creator: Soren Jeppesen, Agnieszka Olenska
item.content:encoded: In the bedding department of Denmark's largest IKEA store, security chief Torben Mortensen walks past rows of display beds and describes a use for them far removed from retail: emergency shelter. If a blackout, flood or attack on critical infrastructure struck, IKEA could turn its stores into emergency shelters or even temporary hospitals. Restaurants could provide meals, generators could keep the buildings running and extra beds could be assembled from flat packs pulled from warehouse shelves. The idea reflects a broader shift in [USN:S8N3P3098 TEXT:"how Europe is thinking"] about security, with governments increasingly looking beyond armed forces and emergency services to businesses that can help keep societies functioning during a crisis. [USN:L8N45F1L2 TEXT:"A wave of"] suspected sabotage, cyber attacks and other incidents that European officials have linked to Russian hybrid warfare has added urgency to those efforts. Denmark's [USN:L8N45G0M0 TEXT:"intelligence service has warned"] Russia is likely to intensify such activities against NATO countries and other Western states in the coming months, an accusation Moscow denies. "We want to be the good neighbour. We want to be the company that can support society in case of a crisis," Mortensen said. The European Union is encouraging member states to work more closely with businesses as part of its Preparedness Union Strategy, launched in March 2025. IKEA is part of Denmark's Corporate Coalition for Crisis Preparedness, a network that catalogues what private firms can provide in an emergency, from beds and food supplies to trucks and specialist staff. "IKEA is a very good example because nobody would put them naturally on a list of crisis resources ... An IKEA store has space, goods, food facilities, and generators," said Maja Broloes, CEO of the network. The concept is not purely theoretical. During [USN:L8N3M90I3 TEXT:"deadly floods"] in Valencia, Spain, in October 2024, IKEA turned one of its stores into a shelter for more than 600 people. The retailer said it did not have a global preparedness programme and that such arrangements were managed country by country. BUSINESS AS BACKUP Other Danish retailers are also preparing for emergencies. Salling Group, Denmark's largest supermarket operator, is opening the first of 51 stores designed to operate for up to 48 hours without electricity or internet access. The trend extends beyond Denmark. Estonia requires 300 companies by law to maintain critical services during a crisis, while Finland has a network of authorities, NGOs and companies responsible for supply security. In Poland, some companies are required by law to let the armed forces use their vehicles, machinery and property in a crisis. The Danish network includes more than 200 companies employing more than 300,000 people, from retailers and construction groups to telecoms providers. "If a crisis hits, the authorities will have one place to ask, and we find companies that can help," Broloes said. She said a state-backed compensation scheme was being established, with reimbursement determined on a case-by-case basis. The voluntary network has taken part in preparedness exercises with government authorities but has yet to face a major real-world emergency. Still, there has already been a glimpse of how a Danish IKEA store might function as a shelter. In December 2021, a snowstorm trapped six customers and about two dozen employees overnight at an IKEA store in Aalborg, forcing them to sleep in the display beds. By the next morning, staff had changed the sheets and reopened the store to shoppers.

item.title: Ex-Deutsche Bank top trader's rate-rigging conviction quashed
item.description: Christian Bittar, a former star Deutsche Bank trader jailed in Britain for conspiring to rig benchmark interest rates, won an appeal to clear his name on Friday, in a fresh blow to the Serious Fraud Office prosecutor.
item.dc:creator: Kirstin Ridley
item.content:encoded: Christian Bittar, a former star Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) trader jailed in Britain for conspiring to rig benchmark interest rates, won an appeal to clear his name on Friday, in a fresh blow to the Serious Fraud Office prosecutor. Bittar was sentenced to five years and four months after pleading guilty in 2018 to conspiring to manipulate Euribor, the Euro Interbank Offered Rate, which helps determine rates on trillions of dollars of financial contracts and loans worldwide. But London's Court of Appeal on Friday quashed the conviction, bringing to six the number of SFO rate-rigging convictions overturned this week alone because of legal errors. Judges will publish their written reasons later. "I have waited a very, very long time for this day," Bittar said in a statement. "Finally, the injustice of what I and others suffered has been recognised. I am so grateful for those who stood by me through this ordeal and those who worked so tirelessly to correct it." Jason Williams, the head of division at the SFO, said the investigator and prosecutor had argued for a different outcome but respected the court's decision. "The SFO remains committed to tackling the most complex fraud, bribery and corruption," he added. BARCLAYS FIVE SEE CONVICTIONS QUASHED Bittar's appeal was heard after senior judges on Wednesday [USN:L8N45T0X8 TEXT:"overturned"] the convictions of five former Barclays (BARC.L) traders, further [USN:L8N3TK0IL TEXT:"unspooling"] some of the SFO's most high-profile prosecutions. Bittar, who earned tens of millions of pounds at Deutsche Bank, is the first person convicted of either manipulating Euribor or Libor, its now-defunct London counterpart, to have seen his conviction overturned following a guilty plea. But his lawyer, Adrian Darbishire, argued that his client's guilty plea was founded on fundamental errors of law, because prosecutors had not been required to prove a factual element of the charge against him - that he had agreed to the submission of "false or misleading" Euribor rates. The derivatives traders were cast by prosecutors as a symbol of banker greed at a time of taxpayer fury at eye-watering bank bailouts following the 2007-2009 credit crisis, which sent stock markets plunging and pitched economies into recession. Launching a criminal investigation in 2012, the SFO prosecuted 20 people. Seven were convicted at trial, two pleaded guilty and 11 were acquitted during a series of tricky London rate-rigging trials and re-trials between 2015 and 2019. Eight of those convictions have now been overturned after the Supreme Court last year [USN:L8N3TK0IL TEXT:"ruled"] that legal errors had undermined the fairness of the first Libor trial - that of former UBS (UBSG.S) and Citigroup (C.N) trader Tom Hayes and a later trial of former Barclays peer, Carlo Palombo. Those errors, which centred on how judges directed the juries, also tarnished later rate-rigging trials, the Court of Appeal ruled on Wednesday.

item.title: Humana surges after topping 2027 Medicare star ratings
item.description: Humana's shares rose 15% on Friday after analysts named it the top beneficiary of the new star ratings for 2027 Medicare Advantage plans, marking a sharp turnaround for the health insurer.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: Humana's (HUM.N) shares rose 15% on Friday after analysts named it the top beneficiary of the new star ratings for 2027 Medicare Advantage plans, marking a sharp turnaround for the health insurer. Humana said 95% of its Medicare Advantage members will be enrolled in plans rated four stars or higher in 2027, up from just [USN:L3N3VQ1HW TEXT:"20% in 2026"], and above J.P. Morgan's expectations of 60% to 70%. Higher ratings from the US health department net insurers billions of dollars in bonus payments from the government. Analysts said Humana's ratings outshine those of larger rivals: J.P. Morgan estimates UnitedHealth's (UNH.N) share of enrollments in plans rated four stars or higher will fall to about 67% from 81% and that of CVS Health (CVS.N) to roughly 70% from 84%. POOR RATINGS IN 2025 AND 2026 Humana had been under pressure since a steep drop in its 2025 ratings threatened its bonus payments. The insurer [USN:L6N3VV0WJ TEXT:"lost a lawsuit"] challenging how the 2025 ratings were calculated in October last year, and forecast 2026 profit [USN:L4N3Z70UI TEXT:"below Wall Street estimates"] in February. Evercore ISI analyst Elizabeth Anderson attributed the sharp rise to improvements in measures of drug-plan quality, health-plan quality and readmissions. The insurer could receive $4.8 billion in bonus payments in 2028 as a result, she said. Baird analysts said the boost to profits will depend on reinvestment in member benefits and arrangements with healthcare providers. Humana is one of the largest providers of Medicare Advantage plans serving people aged 65 and older as well as people with disabilities. Overall, [USN:L4N45U1QK TEXT:"about 71%"] of Medicare Advantage prescription drug plan enrollees are in contracts that will be rated four stars or higher in 2027, the health department said late on Thursday.

item.title: China se compromete a frenar burbujas tecnológicas y controlar riesgos de la IA
item.description: China reforzará la supervisión de su apuesta por la tecnología avanzada, con el objetivo de frenar las burbujas de inversión y garantizar al mismo tiempo que la inteligencia artificial sea "segura, fiable y controlable", según las directrices políticas publicadas el viernes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China reforzará la supervisión de su apuesta por la tecnología avanzada, con el objetivo de frenar las burbujas de inversión y garantizar al mismo tiempo que la inteligencia artificial sea "segura, fiable y controlable", según las directrices políticas publicadas el viernes. Mientras Pekín intensifica su apoyo a la fabricación de alta tecnología y las industrias estratégicas para impulsar la autosuficiencia tecnológica en medio de la rivalidad con Estados Unidos, las directrices advirtieron contra la inversión a ciegas y la expansión excesiva en sectores emergentes. "El desarrollo de nuevas fuerzas productivas es un requisito inherente y un eje importante para promover un desarrollo de alta calidad", según citó la agencia estatal de noticias Xinhua sobre las directrices, publicadas por el Partido Comunista y el Gobierno. El presidente Xi Jinping introdujo el término "nuevas fuerzas productivas" en 2023, haciendo hincapié en la investigación científica, los avances tecnológicos y la modernización industrial en toda la base manufacturera de China. Las directrices indicaron que China buscará avances en la teoría y las tecnologías fundamentales de la IA, reforzará la oferta de potencia de cálculo, algoritmos y datos, y establecerá bases piloto nacionales para aplicaciones industriales de la IA. También abogan por sistemas de seguimiento tecnológico, alerta de riesgos y respuesta ante emergencias para garantizar que la IA siga siendo "segura, fiable y controlable". China aplicará plenamente su iniciativa "IA Plus" para modernizar las industrias tradicionales y acelerar el despliegue de productos inteligentes, incluidos los vehículos conectados de nueva energía, los teléfonos y ordenadores con IA, y los robots humanoides, según el documento. Las directrices también se comprometieron a reforzar la innovación "original y disruptiva" en tecnologías clave y a utilizar el "nuevo sistema nacional" impulsado por el Estado chino para acelerar el desarrollo y el despliegue de productos emblemáticos. Al mismo tiempo, se indicó a los funcionarios que den prioridad a la economía real y eviten las burbujas, el vaciamiento industrial, la inversión a ciegas y las carreras "en masa" hacia los sectores de alta tecnología. China "prohibirá estrictamente el abuso ilegal o indebido de las políticas en nombre del desarrollo de nuevas fuerzas productivas", señalaron las directrices, añadiendo que los funcionarios responsables de pérdidas importantes causadas por inversiones a ciegas tendrán que rendir cuentas. El documento también defiende un desarrollo saludable y ordenado de la "economía de baja altitud" —empresas basadas en drones civiles, taxis aéreos, aeronaves pequeñas y servicios relacionados— garantizando al mismo tiempo la seguridad.

item.title: China vows to curb tech bubbles, keep AI risks in check
item.description: China will tighten oversight of its drive into advanced technology, seeking to curb investment bubbles while ensuring artificial intelligence remains "safe, reliable and controllable", according to policy guidelines issued on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China will tighten oversight of its drive into advanced technology, seeking to curb investment bubbles while ensuring artificial intelligence remains "safe, reliable and controllable", according to policy guidelines issued on Friday. As Beijing ramps up support for high-tech manufacturing and strategic industries to boost technological self-sufficiency amid rivalry with the US, the guidelines warned against blind investment and excessive expansion into emerging sectors. "Developing new productive forces is an inherent requirement and an important focus for promoting high-quality development," Xinhua cited the guidelines, issued by the ruling Communist Party and the cabinet, as saying. President Xi Jinping introduced the term "new productive forces" in 2023, emphasising scientific research, technological breakthroughs and industrial upgrading across China's manufacturing base. The guidelines said China would seek breakthroughs in AI theory and core technologies, strengthen the supply of computing power, algorithms and data, and establish national pilot bases for industrial AI applications. They also called for technology monitoring, risk-warning and emergency-response systems to ensure AI remains "safe, reliable and controllable". China will fully implement its "AI Plus" initiative, using AI to upgrade traditional industries and accelerate the rollout of intelligent products including connected new-energy vehicles, AI-enabled phones and computers, and humanoid robots, the document said. The guidelines also pledged to strengthen "original and disruptive" innovation in core technologies and to use China's state-led "new nationwide system" to speed the development and deployment of landmark products. At the same time, officials were told to prioritise the real economy and avoid bubbles, industrial hollowing-out, blind investment and "swarm-like" rushes into high-tech sectors. China will "strictly prohibit the illegal or improper abuse of policies in the name of developing new productive forces," the guidelines said, adding that officials responsible for major losses caused by blind investment would be held accountable. The document also called for the healthy and orderly development of the low-altitude economy — businesses built around civilian drones, air taxis, small aircraft and related services — while ensuring safety.

item.title: Two men deny carrying out surveillance for Iran of Israeli embassy in UK
item.description: Two Iranian nationals accused of being tasked by Iran to carry out hostile surveillance on the Israeli Embassy in London, Britain's oldest synagogue and other Israeli or Jewish targets pleaded not guilty on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two Iranian nationals accused of being tasked by Iran to carry out hostile surveillance on the Israeli Embassy in London, Britain's oldest synagogue and other Israeli or Jewish targets pleaded not guilty on Friday. Nematollah Shahsavani, 41, and Alireza Farasati, 22, appeared at London's Old Bailey court and denied a single offence under the National Security Act. They were remanded in custody ahead of their trial, which is due to begin in April. The pair are among several individuals who have been charged in separate cases with acting on behalf of Iran in Britain. Britain has recently accused Iran of being behind a [USN:L1N45O076 TEXT:"suspected plot"] targeting the US-linked RAF Fairford military base, with seven men arrested and then [USN:L8N45U0PF TEXT:"released on bail"]. Iran has denied any involvement in hostile activity in Britain, including the alleged RAF Fairford plot, after which the [USN:L1N45R04X TEXT:"US removed its B-1 bombers"] from the base. Shahsavani, a dual Iranian-British national, and Iranian national Farasati are alleged to have gathered information and undertaken reconnaissance in July and August 2025 on behalf of the Iranian intelligence services. Their list of alleged targets included the Israeli Embassy, the Israeli Consulate and London's Bevis Marks Synagogue. Judge Bobbie Cheema-Grubb said one alleged target also included an unnamed individual "of intelligence interest" to Iran. After they were [USN:L1N40709F TEXT:"charged in March"], Britain's Foreign Office said it had [USN:L8N40B1X1 TEXT:"summoned Iran's ambassador"] to the UK.

item.title: Flávio tem 51,1% e Lula 45,7% das intenções de voto no 2º turno, mostra Atlas
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) lidera o segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), rompendo o empate técnico apontado em simulações feitas em levantamentos anteriores, mostrou pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg divulgada nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) lidera o segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), rompendo o empate técnico apontado em simulações feitas em levantamentos anteriores, mostrou pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg divulgada nesta sexta-feira. De acordo com a pesquisa, Flávio registra 51,1% das intenções de voto para o segundo turno, ante 47,4% da pesquisa anterior, enquanto Lula aparece com 45,7%, ante 47,6%. O percentual de eleitores indecisos ou que pretendem votar em branco ou anular o voto caiu para 3,2%, de 5,0% na pesquisa anterior. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 1 ponto percentual para mais ou para menos. Para a pesquisa, contratada pela Bloomberg, o instituto AtlasIntel ouviu 5.026 pessoas online entre os dias 3 e 8 de outubro. Flávio Bolsonaro terminou o primeiro turno da eleição presidencial no último domingo na liderança com 47,03%, contrariando o que apontavam os principais institutos de pesquisa, enquanto Lula obteve 45,16% dos votos.

item.title: Delta Air slashes profit forecast as $6 billion fuel-cost surge outstrips fare gains
item.description: Delta Air Lines cut its annual profit forecast by nearly a quarter on Friday as soaring fuel costs, expected to add $6 billion to its bill in 2026, overwhelmed resilient travel demand and higher ticket prices.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Singh
item.content:encoded: Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) cut its annual profit forecast by nearly a quarter on Friday as soaring fuel costs, expected to add $6 billion to its bill in 2026, overwhelmed resilient travel demand and higher ticket prices. Its shares fell 2.5% in early trading after the carrier cut its 2026 profit forecast for the first time this year and lifted its projected fuel-cost increase by $2 billion as the Iran war has driven jet fuel prices sharply higher worldwide. With no end to the war in sight, carriers are confronting their worst crisis since the pandemic. The downgrade underscores a growing challenge for the industry: whether passengers will absorb further fare increases if fuel prices remain elevated. Airlines have already raised fares substantially this year and analysts warn further increases could test travelers' willingness to keep spending. Delta, the first major global carrier to report third-quarter results, said fuel expenses for the period rose 62% from a year earlier to $4.1 billion, exceeding its July forecast by more than $500 million. "All of it's fuel," Delta Chief Financial Officer Erik Snell told reporters when asked what drove the forecast cut, citing increases in both crude oil and refined jet fuel prices since the summer. Delta now expects adjusted annual earnings of $5.10 to $5.60 a share, down from the $6.50 to $7.50 per share it forecast in July. The new midpoint of $5.35 per share is below analysts' average estimate of $5.46 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. It forecast $4.5 billion in adjusted pre-tax profit for 2026. Third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.72 a share narrowly missed analysts' average estimate of $1.76 apiece, according to data compiled by LSEG. Its adjusted operating margin fell to 9.4% from 11.1%. Rivals United Airlines (UAL.O) , American Airlines (AAL.O) and Southwest Airlines (LUV.N) are due to report later this month. Ryanair Group (RYA.I) CEO Michael O'Leary [USN:L6N45U0JC TEXT:"warned"] on Thursday that European airlines could face more than another year of elevated fuel costs due to the war. HIGHER FARES US airlines spent $42.9 billion on fuel for scheduled flights in the first eight months of 2026, nearly $13.2 billion more than a year earlier, despite using slightly less fuel, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics. Strong demand and limited growth in seats have helped carriers pass higher fuel costs on to passengers. US airline fares rose an average of about 25% from a year earlier in the five months through August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' consumer price index. With fuel prices remaining elevated and planned industry capacity growth set to accelerate in the fourth quarter from the third, analysts are watching whether carriers, including Delta, can raise fares further without discouraging travel. Deutsche Bank analysts expect the industry to recover a smaller share of higher fuel costs through revenue measures in the fourth quarter, with full recovery not expected until early 2027. Delta said demand remains strong. With almost 60% of the fourth quarter already booked, it expects revenue growth of about 20% from a year ago, Snell said. "The general sentiment from our experts is that much of the revenue results and outlooks are held up by the premium passenger and higher fares," Third Bridge analyst Liam Dorsey said. "At the moment, those higher prices have not destroyed any demand and it remains to be seen how long that will last." REFINERY ADVANTAGE Delta has an advantage over other major US airlines: [USN:L4N4051W8 TEXT:"its ownership of a refinery"] outside Philadelphia that Snell expects to generate $700 million in profit this year. "We have a refinery that gives us an offset, a partial offset to fuel prices that no one else does," Snell said. Bought in 2012, the Monroe refinery processes crude oil into jet fuel and other products. Delta still pays market prices for fuel transferred to its airline operations, but retains the refining profit within the company. That helps when the gap between crude and refined fuel prices widens, increasing costs for airlines buying from outside suppliers. The protection varies with refining margins, however, and the refinery can lose money when those margins weaken. But the refinery can only partly cushion the impact of higher fuel prices. Even with a projected refinery benefit of 40 cents a gallon, Delta expects its fuel cost to rise to $4.25 a gallon in the fourth quarter from $3.61 in the third. Snell said fuel costs were expected to stay elevated for some time. "Ultimately, fuel will come down. When that is, we're not exactly sure," he said.

item.title: Wall St climbs as oil slips; SpaceX spectrum deal weighs on telecoms
item.description: US stock indexes edged higher on Friday as oil prices retreated on easing Middle East supply concerns, though telecom shares remained under pressure after SpaceX's spectrum acquisition raised competitive concerns across the sector.
